questions.question: As a compliance officer at a commercial bank, which sanctions-related instruments must the bank take into account when following the Government's orders under section 51A of the UAPA and section 12A of the WMD Act?
questions.answer: The bank must take into account other UNSCRs and the lists in the First and Fourth Schedules of the UAPA, 1967, including any amendments, for compliance with those Government orders.
questions.evidence:
the bank shall take into account:
(1) other UNSCRs and
(2) lists in the first schedule and the fourth schedule of UAPA, 1967 and any amendments to the same for compliance with the Government orders on implementation of section 51A of the UAPA and section 12A of the WMD Act.

questions.question: Must a commercial bank account for amendments to the UAPA, 1967 when considering the First and Fourth Schedule lists for compliance with the Government's orders?
questions.answer: Yes. The bank must take into account any amendments to the UAPA, 1967 when ensuring compliance with the Government orders implementing section 51A of the UAPA and section 12A of the WMD Act.
questions.evidence: lists in the first schedule and the fourth schedule of UAPA, 1967 and any amendments to the same for compliance with the Government orders on implementation of section 51A of the UAPA and section 12A of the WMD Act.

unanswerable.question: How many days does a commercial bank have after a new UNSCR or an amendment to the UAPA schedules is notified before it must incorporate the change into its compliance framework?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph requires the bank to take these instruments into account but does not state any notification, implementation, or review deadline.

questions.question: As a commercial bank, what does the RBI require regarding the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Act, 2010 and the rules made under it?
questions.answer: The bank must ensure adherence to the Act’s provisions and the Rules made thereunder.
questions.evidence: The bank shall ensure adherence to the provisions of Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Act, 2010, and Rules made thereunder.

questions.question: As a commercial bank, what further compliance is required when the RBI issues instructions concerning the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Act, 2010?
questions.answer: The bank must comply with any instructions or communications on the matter issued by the RBI from time to time, based on advice received from the Ministry of Home Affairs, Government of India.
questions.evidence: Further, the bank shall also ensure meticulous compliance with any instructions / communications on the matter issued from time to time by the RBI based on advice received from the Ministry of Home Affairs, Government of India.

unanswerable.question: What deadline must a commercial bank meet for reporting its compliance with the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Act, 2010 to the RBI?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph requires adherence to the Act, Rules made thereunder, and relevant RBI instructions, but it does not specify any reporting requirement or deadline.

questions.question: For a commercial bank, how often must its money laundering and terrorist financing risk assessment be reviewed?
questions.answer: The Board, or a Board committee to which it has delegated this power, determines the assessment’s frequency based on the assessment’s outcome, but the bank must review it at least annually.
questions.evidence: Further, the Board or a committee of the Board to which it has delegated power shall determine the periodicity of the risk assessment exercise, in alignment with the outcome of the risk assessment exercise. However, the bank shall review it at least annually.

questions.question: As a compliance officer at a commercial bank, where must the results of our money laundering and terrorist financing risk assessment be reported?
questions.answer: The results must be presented to the Board or the Board committee that has been delegated this responsibility. They must also be made available to competent authorities and self-regulating bodies.
questions.evidence: The bank shall present the outcome of the exercise to the Board or any committee of the Board to which power has been delegated in this regard. The outcome shall also be made available to competent authorities and self-regulating bodies.

unanswerable.question: How many days does a commercial bank have after completing its money laundering and terrorist financing risk assessment to present the results to the Board?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph requires the outcome to be presented to the Board or a delegated Board committee, but it specifies no deadline in days for doing so.

questions.question: As a commercial bank, what must we do when an existing customer has not submitted a PAN, an equivalent e-document, or Form No. 60 by the date notified by the Central Government?
questions.answer: The bank must temporarily cease operations in the account until the customer submits one of those documents. Before doing so, it must give the customer an accessible notice and a reasonable opportunity to be heard.
questions.evidence: failing which the bank shall temporarily cease operations in the account until the customer submits the PAN or equivalent e-documents thereof or Form No. 60. Provided that before temporarily ceasing operations for an account, the bank shall give the customer an accessible notice and a reasonable opportunity to be heard.

questions.question: For a commercial bank's existing customer's loan account, what is permitted if the bank temporarily ceases operations because the PAN or Form No. 60 requirement has not been met?
questions.answer: Only credits are allowed in the loan account. For asset accounts such as loan accounts, temporary ceasing of operations means that only credits may be made.
questions.evidence: In case of asset accounts such as loan accounts, for the purpose of ceasing the operation in the account, only credits shall be allowed.

unanswerable.question: What maximum grace period, in days, may a commercial bank allow an existing customer to submit a PAN or Form No. 60 after the Central Government's notified deadline?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph does not specify any number of days or grace period; it only refers to the date that the Central Government may notify.

questions.question: For a commercial bank that offers at-par cheque facilities to co-operative banks, what monitoring and risk review must it undertake?
questions.answer: It must monitor the at-par cheque facility and review the arrangements to assess the credit and reputational risks arising from them.
questions.evidence: The ‘at par’ cheque facility offered by the bank to co-operative banks shall be monitored and such arrangements be reviewed to assess the risks including credit risk and reputational risk arising therefrom.

questions.question: For a commercial bank that offers at-par cheque facilities to co-operative banks, what record-verification right must it retain?
questions.answer: It must retain the right to verify the customer co-operative banks’ or societies’ records for compliance with the applicable KYC and AML instructions.
questions.evidence: The right to verify the records maintained by the customer cooperative banks / societies for compliance with the extant instructions on KYC and AML under such arrangements shall be retained by bank.

unanswerable.question: How frequently must a commercial bank review the risks arising from its at-par cheque facility arrangements with co-operative banks?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph requires monitoring and review of the arrangements but does not specify a review frequency, interval, or deadline.

questions.question: For a remittance of ₹50,000 or more, how must a commercial bank fund a demand draft, transfer, or traveller’s cheque?
questions.answer: It must debit the customer’s account or use the customer’s cheques; cash payment is not permitted for the transaction.
questions.evidence: (1) Any remittance of funds by way of demand draft, mail / telegraphic transfer / NEFT / IMPS or any other mode and issue of travellers’ cheques for value of ₹50,000 and above shall be effected by debit to the customer’s account or against cheques and not against cash payment.

questions.question: When must a commercial bank include the purchaser’s name on a demand draft, pay order, or banker’s cheque?
questions.answer: The issuing bank must include the purchaser’s name on the face of the instrument for instruments issued on or after September 15, 2018.
questions.evidence: Further, the bank shall incorporate the name of the purchaser on the face of the demand draft, pay order, banker’s cheque, etc., by the issuing bank. These instructions shall take effect for such instruments issued on or after September 15, 2018.

unanswerable.question: What monetary penalty does a commercial bank incur if it issues a demand draft without the purchaser’s name on its face?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph requires the purchaser’s name to be included and specifies an effective date, but it does not state any penalty for non-compliance.

questions.question: As a commercial bank, what due diligence must we apply to clients and transactions connected to countries that FATF says do not apply its recommendations adequately?
questions.answer: We must apply enhanced due diligence that is effective and proportionate to the risks for business relationships and transactions involving natural and legal persons, including financial institutions, from those countries. We must also give special attention to such relationships and transactions.
questions.evidence: The bank shall apply enhanced due diligence measures, which are effective and proportionate to the risks, to business relationships and transactions with natural and legal persons (including financial institutions) from countries for which this is called for by the FATF.

questions.question: As a commercial bank, what must we examine and retain for transactions involving customers from FATF-listed jurisdictions, and when must we provide the records to regulators?
questions.answer: We must examine the background and purpose of the transactions, retain written findings together with all documents, and make them available to the RBI or other relevant authorities upon request.
questions.evidence: The bank shall examine the background and purpose of transactions with persons (including legal persons and other financial institutions) from jurisdictions included in FATF Statements and countries that do not or insufficiently apply the FATF Recommendations, retain written findings together with all documents, and make them available to the RBI / other relevant authorities, on request.

unanswerable.question: As a commercial bank, how many days must we retain written findings and supporting documents for transactions involving customers from FATF-listed jurisdictions?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph requires retaining written findings and documents and making them available to authorities on request, but it does not specify any retention period or number of days.

questions.question: Under the general restriction, for whom must a commercial bank collect an account payee cheque?
questions.answer: Only for the payee constituent. A commercial bank must not collect an account payee cheque for any other person.
questions.evidence: The bank shall not collect account payee cheques for any person other than the payee constituent.

questions.question: For a co-operative credit society customer of a commercial bank, what cheque-value limit applies when the bank elects to collect an account payee cheque, and what membership condition must the payee meet?
questions.answer: The cheque amount must not exceed ₹50,000, and the named payee must be a constituent of the co-operative credit society whose account is credited.
questions.evidence: The bank shall, at its option, collect account payee cheques drawn for an amount not exceeding ₹50,000 to the account of its customers who are co-operative credit societies, provided the payees of such cheques are the constituents of such co-operative credit societies.

unanswerable.question: Must a commercial bank obtain prior approval from the co-operative credit society before collecting an account payee cheque of ₹50,000 or less?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph permits collection at the bank's option subject to the amount limit and the payee's constituent status, but it does not state any requirement for prior approval from the society.

questions.question: Under the RBI Commercial Banks (KYC) Directions, 2025, when must a commercial bank implement countermeasures requested by an international or intergovernmental organisation?
questions.answer: A commercial bank must implement countermeasures when called upon to do so by an international or intergovernmental organisation of which India is a member and which is accepted by the Central Government.
questions.evidence: The bank shall undertake countermeasures when called upon so to do by any international or intergovernmental organisation of which India is a member and which is accepted by the Central Government.

questions.question: Under the RBI Commercial Banks (KYC) Directions, 2025, what conditions must an international or intergovernmental organisation meet before a commercial bank is required to act on its request for countermeasures?
questions.answer: India must be a member of the organisation, and the organisation must be accepted by the Central Government.
questions.evidence: The bank shall undertake countermeasures when called upon so to do by any international or intergovernmental organisation of which India is a member and which is accepted by the Central Government.

unanswerable.question: Under the RBI Commercial Banks (KYC) Directions, 2025, within how many days must a commercial bank begin implementing countermeasures after an accepted international or intergovernmental organisation calls upon it to do so?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph requires the bank to undertake countermeasures when called upon, but it specifies no deadline or time period for implementation.

questions.question: For a commercial bank, do the RBI's KYC requirements replace its obligations under other laws and regulations, or do they operate in addition to them?
questions.answer: They operate in addition to other laws, rules, regulations, and directions in force; they do not displace or derogate from those obligations.
questions.evidence: The provisions of these Directions shall be in addition to, and not in derogation of the provisions of any other laws, rules, regulations, or directions, for the time being in force.

questions.question: When implementing the RBI's KYC requirements, must a commercial bank continue to comply with other regulatory directions that remain in force?
questions.answer: Yes. The RBI KYC requirements are cumulative, so complying with them does not remove the bank's obligations under other directions in force.
questions.evidence: The provisions of these Directions shall be in addition to, and not in derogation of the provisions of any other laws, rules, regulations, or directions, for the time being in force.

unanswerable.question: If the RBI's KYC requirements for a commercial bank conflict with another law or regulation, which requirement must the bank follow?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph states that the KYC requirements are cumulative and do not derogate from other requirements, but it provides no rule for resolving conflicts or stating which requirement prevails.

questions.question: At a commercial bank, when using the video customer identification process (V-CIP) for CDD of a proprietorship firm, what extra document must we obtain besides identifying the proprietor?
questions.answer: We must also obtain the equivalent electronic document containing the proprietorship firm’s activity proofs, as referred to in paragraphs 31 and 32, in addition to completing CDD of the proprietor.
questions.evidence: Provided that in case of CDD of a proprietorship firm, the bank shall also obtain the equivalent e-document of the activity proofs with respect to the proprietorship firm, as mentioned in paragraph 31 and paragraph 32, apart from undertaking CDD of the proprietor.

questions.question: At a commercial bank, can the video customer identification process (V-CIP) be used to convert an existing account opened in non-face-to-face mode using Aadhaar OTP e-KYC, and to update KYC for eligible customers?
questions.answer: Yes. A commercial bank may use V-CIP both to convert such existing accounts and to carry out KYC updates or periodic KYC updates for eligible customers.
questions.evidence: (2) Conversion of existing accounts opened in non-face-to-face mode using Aadhaar OTP based e-KYC authentication as per paragraph 25. (3) Updation / Periodic updation of KYC for eligible customers.

unanswerable.question: At a commercial bank, within how many days must V-CIP be completed after onboarding a new individual customer?
unanswerable.why: Paragraph 26 permits V-CIP for CDD during new individual-customer onboarding but specifies no deadline or number of days for completing it.

questions.question: Under the RBI's KYC Directions for commercial banks, what must a bank do to keep monitoring its customers after onboarding?
questions.answer: A commercial bank must carry out ongoing due diligence of its customers, checking that customer transactions remain consistent with what the bank knows about the customer, the customer's business and risk profile, and the source of funds or wealth.
questions.evidence: The bank shall undertake ongoing due diligence of customers to ensure that their transactions are consistent with their knowledge about the customers, customers’ business and risk profile, the source of funds / wealth.

questions.question: When a commercial bank performs ongoing due diligence, what customer-related factors must it use to judge whether the transactions are appropriate?
questions.answer: It must assess whether the transactions match the bank's knowledge about the customer, the customer's business and risk profile, and the source of funds or wealth.
questions.evidence: ensure that their transactions are consistent with their knowledge about the customers, customers’ business and risk profile, the source of funds / wealth

unanswerable.question: How frequently must a commercial bank conduct ongoing due diligence on its customers under the RBI KYC Directions, 2025?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph requires ongoing due diligence but does not state any review frequency, interval, or deadline for performing it.

questions.question: For a sole proprietorship customer, how many documents proving the firm's business activity must a commercial bank collect?
questions.answer: A commercial bank must obtain any two of the specified documents (or their equivalent e-documents) as proof of business or activity in the name of the proprietary firm.
questions.evidence: the bank shall also obtain any two of the following documents or the equivalent e-documents thereof as proof of business / activity in the name of the proprietary firm

questions.question: What kinds of documents can a commercial bank accept as proof of business activity for a sole proprietorship?
questions.answer: Acceptable documents include a government registration certificate (including an Udyam Registration Certificate), a municipal Shop and Establishment certificate or licence, sales and income tax returns, a CST/VAT/GST certificate, and other documents listed in the Directions.
questions.evidence: (1) Registration certificate including Udyam Registration Certificate (URC) issued by the Government. (2) Certificate / licence issued by the municipal authorities under Shop and Establishment Act (3) Sales and income tax returns (4) CST / VAT / GST certificate

unanswerable.question: Within what period must a commercial bank obtain the two proof-of-business documents when onboarding a sole proprietorship customer?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph specifies how many documents are required and the types of documents acceptable, but it states no timeframe or deadline for obtaining them.

questions.question: When a commercial bank opens a savings bank account for a Self Help Group (SHG), is customer due diligence of every member required, and whose due diligence is sufficient?
questions.answer: No. A commercial bank need not complete CDD for every SHG member when opening the account; CDD of all office bearers is sufficient.
questions.evidence:
(1) The bank shall not require CDD of all the members of an SHG while opening the savings bank account of the SHG.
(2) The CDD of all the office bearers shall suffice.

questions.question: May a commercial bank undertake customer due diligence of all members of an SHG when the group is linked for credit?
questions.answer: Yes. The bank may undertake CDD of all SHG members at the time of credit linking.
questions.evidence: (3) The bank may undertake CDD of all the members of an SHG at the time of credit linking of SHGs.

unanswerable.question: Within what period must a commercial bank complete CDD of all office bearers of an SHG after opening the group’s savings bank account?
unanswerable.why: The simplified SHG CDD procedure specifies no deadline for completing office-bearer CDD; it only states what is sufficient at account opening and when member CDD may be undertaken.

questions.question: Under the RBI’s KYC Directions for commercial banks, what customer risk categories are required, and what determines the classification?
questions.answer: A commercial bank must classify customers as low, medium, or high risk based on its assessment and risk perception.
questions.evidence: (1) The bank shall categorise customers into low, medium, and high-risk categories, based on its assessment and risk perception.

questions.question: Should a commercial bank disclose a customer’s KYC risk category or explain the reasons for that classification to the customer?
questions.answer: No. The bank must keep both the customer’s risk category and the specific reasons for it confidential to avoid tipping off the customer.
questions.evidence: (4) The bank shall keep the risk categorisation of a customer and the specific reasons for such categorisation confidential and shall not reveal this information to the customer to avoid tipping off.

unanswerable.question: What minimum percentage of customers must a commercial bank classify as high risk under the RBI’s KYC risk-management requirements?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph requires customers to be categorised as low, medium, or high risk, but it does not prescribe any minimum percentage, count, or other numerical threshold for high-risk customers.

questions.question: How often must a commercial bank re-check the risk ratings it assigns to its customer accounts under the RBI's KYC Directions?
questions.answer: At least once every six months, using a system of periodic review that also establishes when enhanced due diligence measures need to be applied.
questions.evidence: The bank shall put in place a system of periodic review of risk categorisation of accounts, with such periodicity being at least once in every six months, and shall establish the need for applying enhanced due diligence measures.

questions.question: If a commercial bank notices a marketing firm asking for a large number of cheque books, or making many small cash deposits from across the country into a single account, what must the bank do?
questions.answer: The bank must immediately report the case to the RBI and other appropriate authorities, such as FIU-IND.
questions.evidence: Cases where a large number of cheque books are sought by the company and / or multiple small deposits (generally in cash) across the country in one bank account and / or where a large number of cheques are issued bearing similar amounts / dates, shall be immediately reported to RBI and other appropriate authorities such as FIU-IND.

unanswerable.question: Within how many days must a commercial bank report a marketing firm's suspicious cheque-book requests or small cash deposit activity to the RBI and FIU-IND?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph requires such cases to be reported immediately but does not state any specific number of days, or any other fixed deadline, for making that report.

questions.question: What must a commercial bank tell customers about the products it offers under the financial education requirement?
questions.answer: A commercial bank must disclose full-fledged information about its products and their implications so that customers can make an informed judgment about their choice.
questions.evidence: A bank shall disclose full-fledged information on its products and their implications to the customers so that the customers can make an informed judgment about their choice of products.

questions.question: To whom must a commercial bank provide full-fledged information about its products and their implications?
questions.answer: It must provide that information to the bank's customers, enabling them to make an informed judgment about their choice of products.
questions.evidence: A bank shall disclose full-fledged information on its products and their implications to the customers so that the customers can make an informed judgment about their choice of products.

unanswerable.question: Within how many days must a commercial bank provide customers with full-fledged information on its products and their implications?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph requires the disclosure but does not specify any time limit, number of days, or other deadline for providing the information.

questions.question: What requirements must a commercial bank meet when renewing an overdue term deposit?
questions.answer: The bank must set out all renewal matters in a transparent, non-discretionary and non-discriminatory policy. It must inform the customer of the renewal terms, including applicable interest rates, when the deposit is accepted.
questions.evidence: All aspects concerning renewal of overdue term deposits shall be laid down in a transparent policy. The policy shall be non-discretionary and non-discriminatory. The terms and conditions of renewal including interest rates shall be notified to the customer at the time of acceptance of deposit.

questions.question: When must a commercial bank disclose the terms and interest rate for renewing an overdue term deposit to the customer?
questions.answer: It must disclose them at the time the customer accepts the deposit.
questions.evidence: The terms and conditions of renewal including interest rates shall be notified to the customer at the time of acceptance of deposit.

unanswerable.question: What grace period must a commercial bank allow before renewing an overdue term deposit?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph requires a transparent, non-discretionary and non-discriminatory renewal policy, but it does not specify any grace period or other deadline for renewal.

questions.question: For a commercial bank, do the RBI's Commercial Banks - Responsible Business Conduct Directions, 2025 replace other laws, rules, regulations, and directions currently in force, or do they apply alongside them?
questions.answer: They apply alongside them. The RBI Directions are additional and do not displace other applicable laws, rules, regulations, or directions in force.
questions.evidence: The provisions of these Directions shall be in addition to, and not in derogation of the provisions of any other laws, rules, regulations, or directions, for the time being in force.

questions.question: Does complying with the RBI's Commercial Banks - Responsible Business Conduct Directions, 2025 excuse a commercial bank from meeting its obligations under other banking laws and regulations?
questions.answer: No. Compliance with the RBI Directions is in addition to, rather than a substitute for, compliance with other applicable laws, rules, regulations, or directions in force.
questions.evidence: The provisions of these Directions shall be in addition to, and not in derogation of the provisions of any other laws, rules, regulations, or directions, for the time being in force.

unanswerable.question: If the RBI's Commercial Banks - Responsible Business Conduct Directions, 2025 conflict with another RBI direction applicable to a commercial bank, which provision must the bank follow?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph states that the Directions do not derogate other laws, rules, regulations, or directions, but it does not specify how conflicts must be resolved or which provision takes priority.

questions.question: As a commercial bank, in which languages must I make printed materials available to retail customers, such as account opening forms, pay-in-slips and passbooks?
questions.answer: You must make all printed material used by retail customers available in three languages: English, Hindi and the concerned Regional Language.
questions.evidence: The bank shall make available all printed material used by retail customers including account opening forms, pay-in-slips, passbooks, etc., in trilingual form, i.e., English, Hindi and the concerned Regional Language.

questions.question: As a commercial bank, what warning do I need to put up at my branches to protect customers from fraudulent deposit schemes?
questions.answer: You must display publicity in your branches cautioning the public against placing deposits in dubious schemes.
questions.evidence: Publicity in the bank branches cautioning public against placing deposits in dubious schemes

unanswerable.question: By what deadline must a commercial bank put up the branch publicity warning customers against depositing money in dubious schemes?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph requires publicity in bank branches cautioning the public against placing deposits in dubious schemes, but it states no date, time period or implementation deadline for doing so.

questions.question: At a commercial bank, what must be in place at branches where we sanction loans secured by gold or silver?
questions.answer: We must provide the necessary infrastructure and facilities and take appropriate security measures at every branch where such loans are sanctioned.
questions.evidence: A bank shall ensure that necessary infrastructure and facilities are put in place and appropriate security measures taken in each of its branches where loans are sanctioned against gold and / or silver collateral.

questions.question: At a commercial bank, where and by whom must gold or silver pledged as loan collateral be handled?
questions.answer: The collateral must be handled only in the bank’s branches and only by the bank’s employees.
questions.evidence: It shall also ensure that the gold and / or silver collateral is handled only in its branches and only by its employees.

unanswerable.question: How many security guards must a commercial bank have on duty at each branch that sanctions loans against gold or silver collateral?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph requires appropriate security measures but does not state any minimum number of guards or another specific security standard.

questions.question: For a commercial bank, which RBI directions govern the interest rates it offers on deposit accounts and related matters?
questions.answer: A commercial bank must be guided by the RBI's instructions on interest rates on deposit accounts and related matters as set out in the Reserve Bank of India (Commercial Banks – Interest Rate on Deposits) Directions, 2025.
questions.evidence: A bank shall be guided by Reserve Bank’s instructions on interest rates on deposit accounts and related matters as prescribed in the Reserve Bank of India (Commercial Banks – Interest Rate on Deposits) Directions, 2025.

questions.question: Does the requirement to follow the RBI's deposit interest-rate instructions under the commercial banks' Responsible Business Conduct Directions extend to lenders outside the commercial bank category, such as small finance banks?
questions.answer: No. The requirement points to the Reserve Bank of India (Commercial Banks – Interest Rate on Deposits) Directions, 2025, so it applies to commercial banks.
questions.evidence: A bank shall be guided by Reserve Bank’s instructions on interest rates on deposit accounts and related matters as prescribed in the Reserve Bank of India (Commercial Banks – Interest Rate on Deposits) Directions, 2025.

unanswerable.question: What minimum balance must a commercial bank require in a savings bank account?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph carries only the heading "A.1 Minimum balance in savings bank accounts" and states no minimum balance amount, formula, or condition; its operative sentence addresses only interest rates on deposit accounts and related matters.

questions.question: If a commercial bank delays settling a deceased customer’s claim involving a safe deposit locker or articles in safe custody beyond the applicable timeline, how much compensation must it pay the claimant for each day of delay?
questions.answer: The bank must pay the claimant(s) ₹5,000 for each day of delay.
questions.evidence: For claims related to safe deposit locker / articles in safe custody, the bank shall be required to pay compensation to the claimant(s) at the rate of ₹5,000 for each day of delay, in cases where it doesn’t adhere to the timeline prescribed in paragraph 320 above.

questions.question: Does the ₹5,000-per-day compensation apply to every deceased-customer claim, or only to claims concerning safe deposit lockers and articles in safe custody?
questions.answer: It applies only to claims related to safe deposit lockers or articles in safe custody, and only when the bank fails to meet the prescribed timeline.
questions.evidence: the bank shall be required to pay compensation to the claimant(s) at the rate of ₹5,000 for each day of delay, in cases where it doesn’t adhere to the timeline prescribed in paragraph 320 above.

unanswerable.question: How many days does a commercial bank have to settle a deceased customer’s claim concerning a safe deposit locker or articles in safe custody before it becomes liable for ₹5,000 per day?
unanswerable.why: The provision specifies the compensation rate but does not state the underlying settlement deadline; it only refers to the timeline prescribed in paragraph 320.

questions.question: What engagement activity should a commercial bank carry out for exporters, and where should it take place?
questions.answer: The bank should periodically organise Exporters' Meet at centres where exporters are concentrated.
questions.evidence: To facilitate interaction between the bank and exporters, the bank should periodically organise Exporters' Meet at centres with concentration of exporters.

questions.question: How often should a commercial bank arrange Exporters' Meet for exporters?
questions.answer: The bank should arrange them periodically, although no fixed interval is specified.
questions.evidence: the bank should periodically organise Exporters' Meet at centres with concentration of exporters.

unanswerable.question: What is the minimum number of Exporters' Meets a commercial bank must organise each year?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph requires periodic organisation of Exporters' Meet but states no annual minimum, fixed frequency, or deadline.

questions.question: As a commercial bank, what must our policy and SOPs for loans secured by gold or silver collateral specify about assessing the pledged items?
questions.answer: They must specify the procedure for assaying gold or silver jewellery, ornaments, or coins and establish qualification criteria for the gold and silver assayer or valuer employed.
questions.evidence: assaying procedure of jewellery, ornaments or coins made of gold or silver (“eligible collateral” for this section); (2) criteria / qualifications for employing gold and silver assayer or valuer;

questions.question: As a commercial bank, what should our policy and SOPs cover when pledged gold or silver collateral is lost, deteriorates, or shows a discrepancy in quantity or purity?
questions.answer: They must prescribe the procedure for addressing the loss or discrepancy, including when identified during internal audit, return, or auction, and provide for fair compensation to the borrower or legal heir with timelines for payment.
questions.evidence: procedure to be followed in case of loss of eligible collateral pledged or any deterioration or discrepancy in quantity or purity of eligible collateral during internal audit or otherwise, including at the time of return or auction of the collateral, and fair compensation to be paid to the borrower(s) / legal heir(s) in such cases, with timelines for effecting the same

unanswerable.question: How many days' notice must a commercial bank give a borrower before auctioning gold or silver collateral pledged for a loan?
unanswerable.why: The provision requires the policy and SOPs to specify the auction-notice timeline and the notice period for settling the loan before auction, but it does not state any number of days.

questions.question: Can a commercial bank offer BSBD account holders extra services beyond the standard minimum, and are charges permitted?
questions.answer: Yes. A commercial bank may offer additional facilities beyond the minimum in a BSBD account, either with or without charges.
questions.evidence: A bank may provide additional facilities beyond the above minimum in a BSBD account, with or without charges

questions.question: What conditions must a commercial bank follow when offering additional services in a BSBD account?
questions.answer: The bank must act without discretion or discrimination, disclose the facilities transparently, avoid requiring any minimum balance in the BSBD account, and leave the customer free to choose whether to use them.
questions.evidence: in a non-discretionary and non-discriminatory manner with transparent disclosure to the customer. However, while doing so, the bank shall not require the customer to maintain a minimum balance in the BSBD account. The availment of such additional facilities shall be at the option of the customer.

unanswerable.question: What is the maximum fee a commercial bank may charge for additional facilities in a BSBD account?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph permits charges but does not specify any maximum fee, fee amount, or charging schedule.

questions.question: For a commercial bank, how often must it review customer accounts that have seen no customer-initiated activity for more than a year?
questions.answer: At least once a year. The review requirement is triggered where there has been no customer-induced transaction in the account for more than one year.
questions.evidence: A bank shall undertake at least an annual review in respect of accounts, where there is no customer-induced transaction for more than a year.

questions.question: As a commercial bank compliance officer, what must the written alert sent to a holder of a long-inactive account tell the customer about continued inactivity and reactivation?
questions.answer: It must state that the account would become 'inoperative' if no operations are carried out during the next one year, and that the account holder would have to submit KYC documents afresh to reactivate the account in that case.
questions.evidence: The alert messages shall invariably mention that the account would become ‘inoperative’ if no operations are carried out during the next one year and, the account holder would be required to submit KYC documents afresh for reactivating the account in such case.

unanswerable.question: What monetary penalty or supervisory action does a commercial bank face if it fails to conduct the annual review of inactive accounts or to send the required alert to the account holder?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph prescribes the annual review and the content and mode of the customer alert, but it does not state any penalty, fine, or supervisory consequence for a bank that fails to comply.

questions.question: As a commercial bank, where can we display warnings about dubious deposit schemes so that customers can easily notice them?
questions.answer: A commercial bank may, wherever feasible, display or distribute the messages in its branches in the official language of the state to enable easy notice by customers.
questions.evidence: Wherever feasible, such messages may be displayed or distributed in the bank branches (in the official language of the state) to enable easy notice by customers.

questions.question: For a commercial bank, are warnings about fraudulent deposit schemes required at ATMs and Business Correspondent Points, or are those locations optional?
questions.answer: They are optional. A commercial bank may consider ATMs and Business Correspondent Points as places to give the messages wider visibility.
questions.evidence: The bank may consider places like ATMs or Business Correspondent Points where such messages could get wider visibility.

unanswerable.question: How frequently must a commercial bank display or distribute these anti-fraud messages in its branches?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph does not specify a frequency, deadline, or mandatory schedule for displaying or distributing the messages.

questions.question: Who bears responsibility for the conduct of recovery agents that a commercial bank hires to collect its dues?
questions.answer: The commercial bank bears responsibility for its agents' actions, acting as principal. It cannot shift that responsibility to the recovery agents it engages.
questions.evidence: The bank, as principal, is responsible for the actions of its agents.

questions.question: What must a commercial bank do to ensure that the recovery agents it engages follow the prescribed recovery instructions?
questions.answer: The bank must ensure that its agents engaged for recovering its dues strictly adhere to the applicable instructions throughout the recovery process.
questions.evidence: it shall ensure that its agents engaged for recovery of its dues strictly adhere to the above instructions, while engaged in the process of recovery of dues.

unanswerable.question: What is the maximum number of recovery agents a commercial bank may engage for recovering its dues?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph places responsibility on the bank for its agents' conduct but states no numerical cap, limit, or condition on how many recovery agents may be engaged.

questions.question: For a commercial bank's branch, where in the banking hall should the customer enquiry or "May I Help You" counter be located, and is it required at every branch?
questions.answer: It must be located near the entry point of the banking hall, and it is required at all branches other than very small branches.
questions.evidence: A bank shall have “Enquiry” or “May I Help You” counters either exclusively or combined with other duties, located near the entry point of the banking hall, at all branches (excluding very small branches).

questions.question: Can a commercial bank's enquiry or "May I Help You" counter also handle other duties, or must it be dedicated solely to assisting customers?
questions.answer: Either arrangement is permitted: the counter may be exclusively for enquiries or may be combined with other duties.
questions.evidence: A bank shall have “Enquiry” or “May I Help You” counters either exclusively or combined with other duties

unanswerable.question: What criteria or size threshold does the RBI use to decide whether a commercial bank branch counts as a "very small branch" that is exempt from having an enquiry or "May I Help You" counter?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph exempts very small branches from the enquiry-counter requirement but does not define that category or state any threshold, number, or condition for it.

questions.question: For a commercial bank handling foreign-currency export bills, from what date should the prescribed post-shipment interest rate stop applying once the foreign currency is credited to the bank's Nostro account?
questions.answer: The prescribed post-shipment interest rate ceases from the date the foreign currency amount is credited to the bank's Nostro account, even though the rupee equivalent has not yet been credited to the exporter's account.
questions.evidence: Although there are instructions that the prescribed post-shipment interest rate will cease from the date of credit to the 'Nostro' account, the credit limits enjoyed by the exporters remain frozen till the actual date of credit of rupee equivalent to the account of the customer.

questions.question: When should a commercial bank restore an exporter's credit limit after realising a foreign-currency export bill?
questions.answer: The bank should promptly restore the exporter's credit limit upon realisation of the bill, instead of keeping the limit frozen until the rupee equivalent is actually credited to the customer's account.
questions.evidence: There is, therefore, a need to promptly restore the limit of the exporters on realisation of bills and pass on the rupee credit to the customer.

unanswerable.question: What amount of compensation must a commercial bank pay an exporter for delayed credit of export bills, and within how many days must the compensation be paid?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph only introduces the heading 'J.1.4 Payment of compensation to exporters for delayed credit of export bills' and states no compensation amount, calculation method, eligibility condition, or payment deadline.

questions.question: What must a commercial bank do periodically to locate customers, nominees, or legal heirs connected with inoperative accounts or unclaimed deposits?
questions.answer: A commercial bank must conduct special drives periodically to determine the whereabouts of customers, their nominees, or legal heirs in relation to inoperative accounts or unclaimed deposits.
questions.evidence: The bank shall undertake special drives periodically to find out the whereabouts of the customers, their nominees or legal heirs in respect of inoperative accounts / unclaimed deposits.

questions.question: Which parties should a commercial bank seek to locate during its periodic special drives concerning inoperative accounts and unclaimed deposits?
questions.answer: It should seek the whereabouts of the customers concerned, their nominees, and their legal heirs.
questions.evidence: The bank shall undertake special drives periodically to find out the whereabouts of the customers, their nominees or legal heirs in respect of inoperative accounts / unclaimed deposits.

unanswerable.question: How frequently must a commercial bank conduct special drives to trace customers, nominees, or legal heirs for inoperative accounts and unclaimed deposits—for example, once every six months or once every year?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph requires special drives periodically but does not specify a fixed frequency, interval, or deadline.

questions.question: As a commercial bank, must we regularly audit service providers, including subcontractors, in relation to the services we outsource?
questions.answer: Yes. Commercial banks must conduct regular audits of service providers, including subcontractors, concerning the services outsourced by them, within the scope of the outsourcing-risk Directions.
questions.evidence: A bank shall conduct regular audits (as applicable to the scope of Directions in this Chapter), of service providers (including subcontractors) with regard to the service outsourced by it.

questions.question: For a commercial bank, who may perform the required audits of outsourced service providers?
questions.answer: The audits may be performed either by the bank’s internal auditors or by external auditors appointed to act on the bank’s behalf.
questions.evidence: Such audits may be conducted either by bank’s internal or external auditors appointed to act on bank’s behalf.

unanswerable.question: How frequently must a commercial bank audit outsourced service providers and their subcontractors under the RBI’s outsourcing-risk Directions?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph requires regular audits but does not specify a frequency, interval, deadline, or minimum number of audits.

questions.question: When a commercial bank appoints a group entity to perform outsourced services, on what basis should it choose that entity?
questions.answer: The commercial bank must base its choice on objective reasons similar to those used when selecting a third-party provider.
questions.evidence: The selection of a group entity shall be based on objective reasons that are similar to selection of a third-party

questions.question: What must a commercial bank do if outsourcing to a group entity creates a conflict of interest?
questions.answer: It must appropriately address the conflict of interest arising from the outsourcing arrangement.
questions.evidence: the bank shall appropriately deal with any conflicts of interest that such an outsourcing arrangement may entail.

unanswerable.question: How long does a commercial bank have to resolve a conflict of interest arising from an outsourcing arrangement with a group entity?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph requires the bank to appropriately deal with such conflicts but does not specify any deadline for resolving them.

questions.question: At a commercial bank, does outsourcing an activity reduce the bank's obligations to customers and the RBI, and who remains ultimately responsible for that activity?
questions.answer: No. Outsourcing does not diminish the bank’s obligations to customers or RBI, and the Board and Senior Management remain ultimately responsible for the outsourced activity.
questions.evidence: As stated in paragraph 9, the outsourcing of any activity by a bank shall not diminish its obligations including to its customers and RBI, and those of its Board and Senior Management, who have the ultimate responsibility for the outsourced activity.

questions.question: When a commercial bank outsources work to direct sales agents, direct marketing agents, or recovery agents, what control must it retain, and for whose actions is it responsible?
questions.answer: The bank must retain ultimate control over the outsourced activity and is responsible for its service provider’s actions, including those of DSAs, DMAs and recovery agents, as well as the confidentiality of customer information held by the provider.
questions.evidence: The bank shall, therefore, be responsible for the actions of its service provider including Direct Sales Agents (DSAs) / Direct Marketing Agents (DMAs) and recovery agents, and the confidentiality of information pertaining to the customers that is available with the service provider. The bank shall retain ultimate control of the outsourced activity.

unanswerable.question: Must a commercial bank perform a minimum percentage of its outsourced activities in-house to retain ultimate control, and if so, what percentage?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph requires the bank to retain ultimate control of outsourced activity, but it states no minimum in-house share or percentage threshold.

questions.question: As a commercial bank, may we engage an outsourcing service provider outside our group if it is owned or controlled by one of our directors, key managerial personnel, or the person approving the outsourcing arrangement, or their relatives?
questions.answer: No. A commercial bank must ensure that a service provider outside its group is not owned or controlled by any of those specified persons or their relatives.
questions.evidence: a bank shall ensure that the service provider, if not a group company, shall not be owned or controlled by any director, or key managerial personnel, or approver of the outsourcing arrangement of the bank, or their relatives.

questions.question: Can a commercial bank make an exception if a non-group-company outsourcing provider is owned or controlled by a director, key managerial personnel, or the outsourcing arrangement's approver, or their relatives?
questions.answer: Yes. The exception requires approval by the Board or a Board Committee, together with appropriate disclosure, oversight and monitoring of the arrangement.
questions.evidence: Provided that an exception to the above requirement may be made with the approval of Board or a Committee of the Board, followed by appropriate disclosure, oversight and monitoring of such arrangements.

unanswerable.question: For a commercial bank, what minimum ownership percentage in a non-group-company outsourcing service provider would trigger the prohibition on the provider being owned by a director, key managerial personnel, the arrangement's approver, or their relatives?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph states no numerical ownership threshold. It prohibits such ownership or control and assigns the meanings of specified terms to the Companies Act, 2013 and the Rules framed thereunder, but does not itself provide a percentage.

questions.question: Our commercial bank runs outsourced services on a multi-tenant IT platform. How can we satisfy the RBI requirement that the bank's data and its customers' data are not combined or comingled with other users' data?
questions.answer: The bank should clearly separate and isolate its own data and its customer-specific data and information, and ensure that access is restricted to personnel the bank has authorised.
questions.evidence: it would suffice if there is clear separation and isolation of data (bank, and its customer specific data and information) to ensure that only the personnel as authorised by the bank is able to access data that belongs to them in a multi-tenant environment / architecture.

questions.question: In a multi-tenant outsourcing environment used by a commercial bank, who is permitted to access the bank's data and its customers' data and information?
questions.answer: Only personnel authorised by the bank may access the data belonging to the bank and its customers.
questions.evidence: only the personnel as authorised by the bank is able to access data that belongs to them in a multi-tenant environment / architecture

unanswerable.question: By what deadline must a commercial bank put in place clear separation and isolation of its data and customer data in a multi-tenant outsourcing arrangement?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph explains how data separation and access restriction can be achieved in a multi-tenant environment, but it states no implementation deadline, time period, or date for doing so.

questions.question: If a commercial bank outsources services to a third-party vendor, is it still required to preserve its customers' rights to seek redressal from the bank?
questions.answer: Yes. Outsourcing arrangements must not affect customers' rights against the bank, including their ability to obtain redressal as applicable under relevant laws.
questions.evidence: Outsourcing arrangements entered into by a bank shall not affect the rights of its customers against the bank, including the ability of the customers to obtain redressal as applicable under relevant laws.

questions.question: Can a commercial bank turn down a customer's complaint about a service merely because that service was delivered by an outsourced vendor?
questions.answer: No. The bank cannot rely on outsourcing to diminish customers' rights against it, which include the ability to obtain redressal as applicable under relevant laws.
questions.evidence: Outsourcing arrangements entered into by a bank shall not affect the rights of its customers against the bank, including the ability of the customers to obtain redressal as applicable under relevant laws.

unanswerable.question: Within how many days must a commercial bank resolve a customer's grievance concerning an outsourced service?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph only requires that outsourcing arrangements not affect customers' rights to redressal under relevant laws; it states no time limit, deadline, or grievance-resolution procedure.

questions.question: What should a commercial bank require in its outsourcing contract so that service-provider risks are managed and problems are corrected promptly?
questions.answer: The contract should require regular and continuous monitoring and assessment of the service provider by the bank, so that necessary corrective measures can be taken immediately.
questions.evidence: (iii) regular and continuous monitoring, and assessment by the bank of the service provider for continuous management of the risks holistically, so that any necessary corrective measure can be taken immediately;

questions.question: What access rights should a commercial bank’s outsourcing contract give RBI to information held by the service provider, including where a foreign bank’s Indian operations are outsourced?
questions.answer: The contract should give RBI, or persons authorized by it, access within a reasonable time to the bank’s documents, transaction records and other necessary information held or processed by the service provider. This also applies when a foreign bank’s controlling or head office outsources activities related to its Indian operations.
questions.evidence: (viii) right of RBI or persons authorised by it to access the bank’s documents, records of transactions, and other necessary information given to, stored or processed by the service provider within a reasonable time; including in cases where the controlling / Head Offices of foreign banks operating in India outsource the activities related to the Indian operations;

unanswerable.question: How many days’ notice must a commercial bank give before terminating an outsourcing agreement?
unanswerable.why: The rule requires a termination clause and a minimum period for executing termination, but it does not specify a notice period, number of days, or other duration.

questions.question: Can a commercial bank outsource any IT service to an entity within its own business group or conglomerate?
questions.answer: Yes. A commercial bank may outsource any IT service within its business group or conglomerate, provided the arrangement is backed by a Board-approved policy and appropriate SLAs or agreements with the group entities are in place.
questions.evidence: A bank may outsource any IT service within its business group / conglomerate, provided that such an arrangement is backed by the Board-approved policy and appropriate SLAs / agreements with its group entities are in place.

questions.question: What must a commercial bank have in place before it outsources an IT service to a group entity?
questions.answer: The outsourcing arrangement must be backed by a Board-approved policy, and appropriate SLAs or agreements must be in place with the group entities.
questions.evidence: provided that such an arrangement is backed by the Board-approved policy and appropriate SLAs / agreements with its group entities are in place.

unanswerable.question: What is the maximum percentage of a commercial bank's IT services that may be outsourced to entities within its business group or conglomerate?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph permits outsourcing of any IT service within the group but sets no percentage cap, limit, or other quantitative threshold on such intra-group outsourcing.

questions.question: If my commercial bank and another lender both outsource IT services to the same third-party service provider, can we carry out a joint audit instead of each one auditing the provider separately?
questions.answer: Yes. Where more than one RE uses the same third-party service provider, they may adopt a pooled (shared) audit in place of separate audits by each RE. They can either pool their own audit resources or engage an independent third-party auditor to jointly audit the common service provider.
questions.evidence: While outsourcing various IT services, more than one RE may be availing services from the same third-party service provider. In such scenarios, in lieu of conducting separate audits by individual REs of the common service provider, they may adopt pooled (shared) audit.

questions.question: If my commercial bank participates in a shared audit of a common outsourced service provider, am I still accountable for ensuring my own contract's audit requirements are satisfied?
questions.answer: Yes. Even when a pooled or jointly conducted audit is used, each RE remains responsible for ensuring that the audit requirements tied to its own contract with the service provider are effectively met.
questions.evidence: However, in doing so, it shall be the responsibility of REs in ensuring that the audit requirements related to their respective contract with the service provider are met effectively.

unanswerable.question: How frequently must a commercial bank conduct a pooled audit of a common third-party service provider under the RBI's outsourcing risk directions?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph permits pooled (shared) audits and places responsibility on REs for their contract-specific audit requirements, but it does not state any audit frequency, interval, or deadline for conducting such audits.

questions.question: What additional factors must a commercial bank consider when evaluating a service provider for outsourced IT services?
questions.answer: In addition to the general service-provider evaluation criteria, the bank must consider technology and infrastructure stability, backup and disaster recovery arrangements, conflicts of interest, the provider’s ability to segregate bank data and meet regulatory and legal requirements, and information and cyber security risks.

questions.question: What must a commercial bank ensure through controls, assurance requirements, and contracts for data handled by an outsourced IT service provider?
questions.answer: The bank must ensure that appropriate controls, assurance requirements, and possible contractual arrangements protect the data and preserve the bank’s access to data processed, managed, or stored by the service provider.
questions.evidence: (vi) ensuring that appropriate controls, assurance requirements, and possible contractual arrangements are in place to ensure data protection and bank’s access to the data which is processed, managed or stored by the service provider;

unanswerable.question: How frequently must a commercial bank reassess an outsourced IT service provider’s information and cyber security risks?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph requires information and cyber security risk assessment but does not specify any reassessment frequency or deadline.

questions.question: What records must a commercial bank maintain for the IT services it outsources, including important participants in its providers’ supply chains?
questions.answer: A commercial bank must maintain an inventory of outsourced IT services that includes key entities involved in the service providers’ supply chains.
questions.evidence: A bank shall create an inventory of IT services outsourced to service providers (including key entities involved in their supply chains).

questions.question: What must a commercial bank do to understand its reliance on outside providers and assess the information they provide?
questions.answer: It must map its dependency on third parties and periodically evaluate the information received from service providers.
questions.evidence: Further, the bank shall map its dependency on third parties and periodically evaluate the information received from the service providers.

unanswerable.question: How many key supply-chain entities must a commercial bank include in its inventory of outsourced IT services?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph requires the inclusion of key entities involved in service providers’ supply chains but does not specify a minimum number.

questions.question: What must a commercial bank consider when building a contingency plan for an outsourced activity?
questions.answer: It must consider whether alternative service providers are available or whether the outsourced activity could be brought back in-house during an emergency, along with the costs, time, and resources that each option would involve.
questions.evidence: In establishing a viable contingency plan, a bank shall consider the availability of alternative service providers or the possibility of bringing the outsourced activity back in-house in an emergency, and the costs, time, and resources that would be involved.

questions.question: If a commercial bank plans to fall back on another service provider or resume an outsourced function internally during an emergency, what does it need to weigh?
questions.answer: It needs to weigh the availability of alternative service providers or the feasibility of bringing the outsourced activity back in-house in an emergency, and the costs, time, and resources that would be involved.
questions.evidence: the availability of alternative service providers or the possibility of bringing the outsourced activity back in-house in an emergency, and the costs, time, and resources that would be involved.

unanswerable.question: How often must a commercial bank test and update its contingency plan for outsourced activities?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph requires a commercial bank to consider alternative service providers, returning the activity in-house in an emergency, and the related costs, time, and resources, but it sets no testing or review frequency, deadline, or other numeric requirement.

questions.question: As a commercial bank, what must the Board or its delegated Committee do to oversee outsourcing arrangements?
questions.answer: It must establish a framework to assess the risks and materiality of all existing and prospective outsourcing arrangements, set approval authorities based on those risks and materiality, and conduct regular reviews.
questions.evidence: shall be responsible for putting in place a framework to evaluate the risks and materiality of all existing and prospective outsourcing arrangements, laying down appropriate approval authorities depending on risks and materiality, and undertaking regular review.

questions.question: For a commercial bank, which body is accountable for establishing the outsourcing risk framework and setting approval authorities?
questions.answer: Accountability rests with the Board or a Committee of the Board to which powers have been delegated, as applicable for financial or IT outsourcing.
questions.evidence: The Board or a Committee of the Board to which powers have been delegated, as applicable for financial or IT outsourcing, shall be responsible for putting in place a framework to evaluate the risks and materiality

unanswerable.question: For a commercial bank, how frequently must outsourcing arrangements be reviewed?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph requires regular review but does not specify a review interval, frequency, or deadline.

questions.question: As a commercial bank, if our outsourced service provider wants to pass part of the work to a subcontractor, do the RBI outsourcing requirements still apply, and what must we do before agreeing to it?
questions.answer: Yes — the requirements extend, mutatis mutandis, to subcontracted activities, and the outsourcing contract must provide for the bank's prior approval or consent before the service provider engages any subcontractor. Before granting consent, the bank must review the subcontracting arrangement and ensure it complies with Chapter III of the Directions.
questions.evidence: The provisions shall also apply, mutatis mutandis, to subcontracted activities. For this purpose, the outsourcing contract shall provide for prior approval or consent of the bank before a service provider engages any subcontractor for all or part of the outsourced activity.

questions.question: As a commercial bank, which outsourced activities fall outside the scope of the RBI's outsourcing requirements?
questions.answer: Excluded are IT services (as defined in paragraph 53(1)) unless Chapter IV states otherwise, activities unrelated to banking services such as courier use, staff catering, housekeeping and janitorial services, premises security, and movement and archiving of records, and audit-related assignments to Chartered Accountant firms, which remain governed by Department of Supervision, RBI instructions.
questions.evidence: The provisions shall not apply to outsourcing of: (i) IT services as defined in paragraph 53(1) of these Directions, unless specified otherwise in respective paragraphs of Chapter IV; (ii) activities unrelated to banking services like usage of courier, catering of staff, housekeeping and janitorial services

unanswerable.question: What is the maximum share of a commercial bank's outsourced financial services that may be subcontracted without the bank's prior approval under the RBI outsourcing framework?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph requires the bank's prior approval or consent before a service provider engages any subcontractor, but it states no percentage, numerical cap, or other quantitative limit on subcontracting.

questions.question: As a commercial bank, can we outsource our internal audit function to an external service provider?
questions.answer: No. A commercial bank may outsource financial services, but internal audit is a core management function that must not be outsourced.
questions.evidence: A bank which chooses to outsource financial services shall however not outsource core management functions including Internal Audit, compliance function, and decision-making functions like determining compliance with KYC norms for opening deposit accounts, giving sanction for loans (including retail loans), and management of investment portfolio.

questions.question: As a commercial bank, can we outsource decisions on whether to sanction retail loans?
questions.answer: No. Deciding whether to sanction loans, including retail loans, is a core management decision-making function that a commercial bank must not outsource.
questions.evidence: A bank which chooses to outsource financial services shall however not outsource core management functions including Internal Audit, compliance function, and decision-making functions like determining compliance with KYC norms for opening deposit accounts, giving sanction for loans (including retail loans), and management of investment portfolio.

unanswerable.question: Is there a percentage limit on the proportion of a commercial bank's activities that may be outsourced?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph prohibits outsourcing specified core management functions but does not state any numerical limit on the proportion of activities that may be outsourced.

questions.question: As a commercial bank, what must we have in place to manage the risks arising from outsourced IT services?
questions.answer: We must have a comprehensive risk management framework covering the processes and responsibilities for handling risks arising from IT outsourcing arrangements.
questions.evidence: A bank shall put in place a risk management framework that comprehensively deals with the processes and responsibilities for identification, measurement, mitigation, management, and reporting of risks associated with such IT outsourcing arrangements.

questions.question: Which risk-management activities must a commercial bank's framework cover for IT outsourcing arrangements?
questions.answer: It must cover identification, measurement, mitigation, management, and reporting of the risks associated with IT outsourcing arrangements.
questions.evidence: the processes and responsibilities for identification, measurement, mitigation, management, and reporting of risks associated with such IT outsourcing arrangements.

unanswerable.question: How frequently must a commercial bank review and report on risks arising from outsourced IT arrangements?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph requires a framework that includes risk reporting, but it does not state any reporting frequency, review interval, or deadline.

questions.question: Does the RBI credit card and debit card issuance and conduct framework apply to the State Bank of India?
questions.answer: Yes. The State Bank of India is expressly included within the definition of commercial banks covered by the framework.
questions.evidence: For the purpose of these Directions, ‘Commercial Banks’ mean banking companies (other than Small Finance Banks, Payment Banks, and Local Area Banks), corresponding new banks, and the State Bank of India, as defined respectively under clauses (c), (da), and (nc) of Section 5 of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949.

questions.question: If my company is a banking company but not a small finance bank, payment bank, or local area bank, is it covered by the RBI's credit card and debit card issuance and conduct requirements?
questions.answer: Yes. Banking companies other than small finance banks, payment banks, and local area banks fall within the commercial bank category covered by the framework.
questions.evidence: ‘Commercial Banks’ mean banking companies (other than Small Finance Banks, Payment Banks, and Local Area Banks), corresponding new banks, and the State Bank of India, as defined respectively under clauses (c), (da), and (nc) of Section 5 of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949.

unanswerable.question: What minimum net worth must a banking company have to qualify for the RBI's credit card and debit card issuance and conduct requirements?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph identifies covered lenders by their statutory category and excludes small finance banks, payment banks, and local area banks; it states no minimum net worth or other financial threshold.

questions.question: What must a commercial bank do to ensure that card complaints handled by its call centre are addressed competently and escalated when needed?
questions.answer: The bank must adequately train its call-centre staff to handle complaints and escalate them when necessary. Its grievance process must also automatically send unresolved complaints from the call centre or base level to higher authorities.
questions.evidence: Card-issuers shall ensure that their call centre staff are trained adequately to competently handle and escalate, a complaint, if necessary. The Grievance Redressal process shall have a provision for automatic escalation of unresolved complaints from a call center / base level to higher authorities.

questions.question: What should a commercial bank provide when a customer reports a card complaint by telephone so that the issue can be tracked for follow-up?
questions.answer: The bank should provide an acknowledgement for follow-up, such as a complaint number or docket number, even for complaints received by phone.
questions.evidence: There shall be a system of acknowledging customers' complaints for follow up, such as complaint number / docket number, even if the complaints are received over phone.

unanswerable.question: Within what period must a commercial bank acknowledge a card complaint received by telephone?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph requires an acknowledgement or tracking number for telephone complaints but does not specify any deadline for providing it.

questions.question: As a commercial bank issuing a co-branded credit or debit card, what must the card itself disclose about the arrangement?
questions.answer: The card must explicitly indicate that it has been issued under a co-branding arrangement.
questions.evidence: The co-branded card shall explicitly indicate that the card has been issued under a cobranding arrangement.

questions.question: For a commercial bank's co-branded card campaign, may the co-branding partner promote the card as its own product, and how must the issuing bank be identified in the advertising?
questions.answer: No. The co-branding partner may not advertise or market the card as its own product, and the card-issuer's name must be clearly shown in all marketing or advertising material.
questions.evidence: The co-branding partner shall not advertise / market the cobranded card as its own product. In all marketing / advertising material, the name of the card-issuer shall be clearly shown.

unanswerable.question: For a commercial bank's co-branded card, what minimum percentage of the marketing material must display the issuing bank's name?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph requires the card-issuer's name to be clearly shown in all marketing or advertising material but specifies no percentage or other numeric threshold.

questions.question: As a commercial bank that issues credit cards, what must we and our collection agents avoid when trying to recover an overdue card balance?
questions.answer: The bank and its agents must not intimidate or harass anyone, verbally or physically, during debt collection efforts.
questions.evidence: Card-issuers / their agents shall not resort to intimidation or harassment of any kind, either verbal or physical, against any person in their debt collection efforts

questions.question: For a commercial bank’s credit card collections, are threatening or anonymous calls, false claims, public humiliation, and privacy intrusions involving a cardholder’s family, friends, or referees prohibited?
questions.answer: Yes. All these practices are prohibited during credit card debt collection.
questions.evidence: including acts intended to humiliate publicly or intrude upon the privacy of the credit cardholders’ family members, referees and friends, making threatening and anonymous calls or making false and misleading representations.

unanswerable.question: For a commercial bank issuing credit cards, what is the maximum number of debt-collection calls permitted for each customer in a day?
unanswerable.why: Paragraph 39 prohibits intimidation, harassment, threatening or anonymous calls, and false or misleading representations, but it does not specify any numerical limit on collection-call frequency.

questions.question: As a commercial bank, can we issue co-branded debit, prepaid, and credit cards without obtaining the Reserve Bank's prior approval?
questions.answer: Yes. A commercial bank may issue these co-branded cards without prior Reserve Bank approval, provided it complies with the conditions in the co-branding chapter and the conditions applicable to the relevant card type.
questions.evidence: Prior approval of the Reserve Bank is not necessary for the issuance of co-branded debit cards, co-branded prepaid cards and co-branded credit cards subject to conditions stipulated under this chapter.

questions.question: Must a commercial bank's co-branded card arrangement satisfy only the co-branding conditions, or are additional card-specific requirements also applicable?
questions.answer: Both apply. The arrangement must comply with the conditions in the co-branding chapter as well as the specific conditions applicable to the relevant card type.
questions.evidence: In addition to the conditions listed herein, the co-branding arrangement for credit cards, debit cards and prepaid cards shall also be subject to the specific conditions applicable to such cards.

unanswerable.question: Does the rule set an annual limit on the number of co-branded debit, prepaid, or credit cards that a commercial bank may issue?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph does not state any annual issuance limit or numerical cap; it addresses prior approval and the applicable conditions.

questions.question: For a commercial bank's credit card account, if a refund or reversed transaction arrives after the customer has already paid the bill, what is the maximum amount the bank can adjust against the credit limit without getting consent first?
