questions.answer: The bank may adjust up to the lower of 1% of the credit limit or ₹5,000. Any amount beyond that cut-off requires the cardholder's explicit consent.
questions.evidence: Card-issuers shall seek explicit consent of the cardholder to adjust credit amount beyond a cut-off, one percent of the credit limit or ₹5000, whichever is lower, arising out of refund / failed / reversed transactions or similar transactions against the credit limit for which payment has already been made by the cardholder.

questions.question: If a commercial bank credit card customer asks the bank to transfer an outstanding credit amount to their bank account, how soon must the bank complete that request?
questions.answer: The bank must reverse the credit amount into the customer's bank account within three working days from receiving the request, even if the amount exceeds the usual adjustment cut-off.
questions.evidence: Notwithstanding the cut-off, if a cardholder makes a request to the card-issuer for reversal of the credit amount outstanding in the card account into his / her bank account, the card-issuer shall do it within three working days from the receipt of such request.

unanswerable.question: May a commercial bank credit card issuer charge the cardholder a fee or penalty if the cardholder does not respond to the consent request within seven days?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph requires consent to be sought and the credit to be reversed when there is no consent or response, but it does not state whether any fee or penalty may be charged for non-response.

questions.question: When a commercial bank card issuer reports a cardholder's credit history or repayment record to a registered Credit Information Company, what must it explicitly tell the customer?
questions.answer: The bank must explicitly bring to the customer's notice that the information is being provided under the Credit Information Companies (Regulation) Act, 2005.
questions.evidence: For providing information relating to credit history / repayment record of the cardholder to a Credit Information Company (that has obtained Certificate of Registration from RBI), the card-issuer shall explicitly bring to the notice of the customer that such information is being provided in terms of the Credit Information Companies (Regulation) Act, 2005.

questions.question: What registration status must an organization have to be eligible to receive a commercial bank cardholder's credit history or repayment record under this reporting requirement?
questions.answer: It must be a Credit Information Company that has obtained a Certificate of Registration from the Reserve Bank of India.
questions.evidence: For providing information relating to credit history / repayment record of the cardholder to a Credit Information Company (that has obtained Certificate of Registration from RBI)

unanswerable.question: How many days in advance must a commercial bank card issuer notify the customer before reporting the cardholder's credit history or repayment record to a registered Credit Information Company?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph requires explicit notice to the customer but does not specify any advance notice period, deadline, or notification frequency.

questions.question: As a commercial bank issuing credit cards, what information must appear in every communication sent by a third-party debt collection agency acting on our behalf?
questions.answer: Every communication from a recovery agent must give the customer the name, email ID, telephone number, and address of the senior officer of the card-issuer whom the customer can contact.
questions.evidence: All communications issued by recovery agents must contain the name, email-id, telephone number and address of the concerned senior officer of the card-issuer whom the customer can contact.

questions.question: When our commercial bank hands a credit card debt collection case to a third-party recovery agency, what must we tell the cardholder and when?
questions.answer: We must provide the cardholder with the name and contact details of the recovery agent immediately upon assigning that agent to the cardholder.
questions.evidence: Further, card-issuers shall provide the name and contact details of the recovery agent to the cardholder immediately upon assigning the agent to the cardholder.

unanswerable.question: For a commercial bank's credit card debt collection, what is the maximum number of times a recovery agent may contact a cardholder in a day, and what cooling-off period must follow each contact?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph sets no limit on the number or frequency of contact attempts by recovery agents, and states no cooling-off period or other numerical condition for such contact.

questions.question: As a commercial bank issuing credit cards, after how many days past due may we report the account to credit information companies or impose a late-payment charge?
questions.answer: We may do so only after the account has remained past due for more than three days. The days past due and late-payment charges are calculated from the payment due date shown on the credit card statement.
questions.evidence: Card-issuers shall report a credit card account as 'past due' to credit information companies (CICs) or levy penal charges, viz. late payment charges and other related charges, if any, only when a credit card account remains 'past due' for more than three days.

questions.question: As a commercial bank issuing credit cards, how should we structure the minimum amount due, and may we charge interest on unpaid taxes or levies?
questions.answer: The minimum amount due must be structured so that repayment does not result in negative amortization. We must not capitalize interest or any other charges on unpaid taxes, levies, or charges.
questions.evidence: The terms and conditions for payment of credit card dues, including the minimum amount due, shall be stipulated so as to ensure there is no negative amortization. Card-issuers shall not capitalize i.e., levy interest or any other charges, on the unpaid taxes/levies/charges.

unanswerable.question: What is the maximum annual percentage rate a commercial bank may charge on a credit card for cash advances?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph requires disclosure of APRs for different situations but does not prescribe any maximum APR or other numerical ceiling.

questions.question: For credit and debit cards issued by a commercial bank, what must happen before the bank can impose a fee that was not disclosed when the card was issued?
questions.answer: The bank must obtain the cardholder’s explicit consent before levying the undisclosed charge.
questions.evidence: Card-issuers shall not levy any charge that was not explicitly indicated to the cardholders at the time of issue of the card and without getting their explicit consent.

questions.question: For a commercial bank, where must customers be able to see the details of all charges associated with its credit and debit cards?
questions.answer: The bank must display those charge details on its website.
questions.evidence: The details of all the charges associated with cards shall be displayed on the card-issuer’s website.

unanswerable.question: For a commercial bank issuing credit cards, what is the maximum annual fee the bank may charge?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph does not specify any numerical cap on card charges.

questions.question: As a commercial bank, may I issue a business credit card to an individual for business-related spending?
questions.answer: Yes. A commercial bank may issue business credit cards to individuals for business expenses.
questions.evidence: Card-issuers may issue business credit cards to business entities / individuals for business expenses.

questions.question: In what forms can a commercial bank issue a business credit card?
questions.answer: It may issue one as a charge card, as a corporate credit card, or by linking a business-purpose overdraft or cash credit facility, subject to that facility’s stipulated terms and conditions.
questions.evidence: The business credit cards may also be issued as charge cards, corporate credit cards or by linking a credit facility such as overdraft / cash credit provided for business purpose as per the terms and conditions stipulated for the facility concerned.

unanswerable.question: What minimum credit limit must a commercial bank set when issuing a business credit card?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph permits business credit cards and describes their forms, but it does not specify any minimum or maximum credit limit.

questions.question: As a commercial bank that issues credit cards, who needs to approve our policy on credit card issuance and conduct, and what must that policy consist of?
questions.answer: The bank must have a well-documented policy for credit card issuance and conduct, and it must be approved by the Board or by a Committee to which the Board has delegated powers.
questions.evidence: Each card-issuer shall have a well-documented policy for the issuance and conduct of credit cards, approved by its Board or any Committee to which powers have been delegated by the Board.

questions.question: As a commercial bank card issuer, where must we publish our credit card issuance and conduct policy?
questions.answer: The policy must be made available on the bank's website.
questions.evidence: The policy shall be available on the website of the card-issuer.

unanswerable.question: Within how many days after Board approval must a commercial bank upload its credit card issuance and conduct policy to its website?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph requires the policy to be available on the card-issuer's website but does not state any deadline, time period, or condition for uploading or publishing it.

questions.question: What must a commercial bank do to prevent inaccurate card bills from reaching cardholders?
questions.answer: It must ensure that wrong bills are neither raised nor issued to cardholders.
questions.evidence: Card-issuers shall ensure that wrong bills are not raised and issued to cardholders.

questions.question: When a commercial bank cardholder disputes a card bill, what must the bank provide, and how quickly?
questions.answer: The bank must provide an explanation and, where applicable, documentary evidence within a maximum of 30 days from the date of the complaint.
questions.evidence: In case, a cardholder protests any bill, the card-issuer shall provide explanation and, wherever applicable, documentary evidence shall be provided to the cardholder within a maximum period of 30 days from the date of complaint.

unanswerable.question: What monetary penalty must a commercial bank pay if it raises or issues a wrong bill to a cardholder?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph imposes duties on card-issuers but does not specify any monetary penalty or other sanction for violating them.

questions.question: As a commercial bank issuing credit or debit cards, what legal basis must govern its relationship with cardholders, and what must it make available to them in writing?
questions.answer: The relationship must be contractual. The bank must make written contractual terms and conditions governing the issue and use of the cards available to cardholders.
questions.evidence: The relationship between the card-issuer and the cardholder shall be contractual. Card-issuers shall make available to the cardholders in writing, a set of contractual terms and conditions governing the issue and use of such cards.

questions.question: What drafting standards must a commercial bank follow when setting the written terms and conditions for its credit or debit cards?
questions.answer: The terms must be expressed clearly and maintain a fair balance between the interests of the parties concerned.
questions.evidence: These terms shall be expressed clearly and also maintain a fair balance between the interests of the parties concerned.

unanswerable.question: Within how many days must a commercial bank make its written card terms and conditions available to a cardholder?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph requires written terms to be made available but does not specify any deadline or number of days for doing so.

questions.question: As a commercial bank, what customer information may we disclose to our DSAs, DMAs, and recovery agents?
questions.answer: You may disclose it only to the extent needed for those agents to perform their duties, and must not release personal information supplied by the cardholder if it is unnecessary for recovery.
questions.evidence: The disclosure of customers’ information to the DSAs / DMAs / recovery agents shall also be limited to the extent that will enable them to discharge their duties. Personal information provided by the cardholder but not required for recovery purposes shall not be released by the card-issuer.

questions.question: What must a commercial bank do to prevent outsourced agents from misusing customer information when marketing credit cards?
questions.answer: The bank must ensure that its DSAs, DMAs, and recovery agents neither transfer nor misuse any customer information during credit card marketing.
questions.evidence: The card-issuer shall ensure that the DSAs / DMAs / recovery agents do not transfer or misuse any customer information during marketing of credit card products.

unanswerable.question: What is the maximum period for which a commercial bank may share cardholder information with a recovery agent?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph does not specify any time limit, renewal requirement, or consent condition for sharing customer information with recovery agents.

questions.question: May a commercial bank determine the interest rate on deposits accepted or renewed under the Resident Foreign Currency (RFC) Account Scheme?
questions.answer: Yes. A commercial bank may determine the interest rate, provided it complies with a comprehensive policy on deposit interest rates approved by the Board of Directors or a Board committee with delegated powers.
questions.evidence: A bank shall have the freedom to determine interest on deposits of money accepted by it or renewed by it under the RFC Account Scheme, in accordance with the comprehensive policy on interest rate on deposits duly approved by the Board of Directors or any Committee of the Board to which powers have been delegated.

questions.question: Under the Resident Foreign Currency (RFC) Account Scheme, who must approve a commercial bank's policy for determining interest on deposits?
questions.answer: The policy must be approved by the Board of Directors or by a Committee of the Board to which the necessary powers have been delegated.
questions.evidence: in accordance with the comprehensive policy on interest rate on deposits duly approved by the Board of Directors or any Committee of the Board to which powers have been delegated.

unanswerable.question: What is the maximum interest rate that a commercial bank may offer on deposits under the Resident Foreign Currency (RFC) Account Scheme?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph gives banks discretion over deposit interest but states no maximum or minimum rate, rate cap, or calculation formula.

questions.question: If a customer of a commercial bank withdraws a domestic term deposit before maturity, on what basis must the bank calculate the interest paid?
questions.answer: The bank must apply the rate applicable to the amount and the period for which the deposit remained with the bank, rather than the originally contracted rate.
questions.evidence: (1) Interest shall be paid at the rate applicable to the amount and period for which the deposit remained with the bank and not at the contracted rate.

questions.question: Must a commercial bank pay interest when a customer prematurely withdraws a domestic term deposit before completing the minimum period specified in paragraph 10(1)?
questions.answer: No. A commercial bank must pay no interest if the premature withdrawal occurs before that minimum period is completed.
questions.evidence: (2) No interest shall be paid, where premature withdrawal of deposit takes place before completion of the minimum period specified in paragraph 10(1).

unanswerable.question: What is the minimum period that a domestic term deposit must complete with a commercial bank before a premature withdrawal can earn interest?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph refers to the minimum period specified in paragraph 10(1), but it does not state the length of that period.

questions.question: As a commercial bank, what minimum maturity must I use for non-resident rupee term deposits under the NRE and NRO schemes?
questions.answer: The minimum tenor is one year for NRE term deposits and seven days for NRO term deposits.
questions.evidence: A bank shall have the freedom to determine the maturity / tenor of the deposit subject to the condition that minimum tenor of NRE term deposits shall be one year and that of NRO term deposits shall be seven days.

questions.question: As a commercial bank, when am I required to let an individual depositor withdraw an NRE or NRO term deposit before maturity?
questions.answer: A premature-withdrawal facility is mandatory for all NRE and NRO term deposits accepted from individuals, whether held singly or jointly, for amounts of ₹1 crore or less.
questions.evidence: Provided that all NRE / NRO term deposits accepted from individuals (held singly or jointly) for amount of ₹1 crore and below shall have premature withdrawal facility.

unanswerable.question: As a commercial bank, what exact interest rate should I offer on an NRO term deposit with the minimum seven-day tenor?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph specifies a seven-day minimum tenor for NRO term deposits and rules governing rate differentiation, but it does not state the actual interest rate or a numerical rate schedule for that product.

questions.question: What must a commercial bank have in place before it can accept rupee deposits from non-residents under NRE and NRO accounts?
questions.answer: The bank must be authorised under FEMA by the Reserve Bank of India from time to time.
questions.evidence: Rupee deposits of non-residents under NRE and NRO deposits shall be accepted only by those banks that are authorised under Foreign Exchange Management Act,1999 (FEMA) by Reserve Bank of India from time to time.

questions.question: Can a commercial bank without RBI authorisation under FEMA accept rupee deposits from non-residents under NRE and NRO accounts?
questions.answer: No. Only banks authorised under FEMA by the RBI may accept such deposits.
questions.evidence: Rupee deposits of non-residents under NRE and NRO deposits shall be accepted only by those banks that are authorised under Foreign Exchange Management Act,1999 (FEMA) by Reserve Bank of India from time to time.

unanswerable.question: What maximum interest rate may a commercial bank offer on NRE and NRO rupee deposits from non-residents?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph specifies which banks may accept these deposits but does not state any interest rate, maximum rate, or rate-calculation condition.

questions.question: For a commercial bank, can it choose to pay an extra 1% per year on eligible staff members’ savings or term deposits?
questions.answer: Yes. A commercial bank may, at its discretion, pay an additional 1% per annum above the scheduled rate on eligible staff members’ savings or term deposits.
questions.evidence: A bank shall, at its discretion, allow additional interest of one per cent per annum, over and above the rate of interest mentioned in the schedule of interest rates on savings or term deposits to bank’s staff and their exclusive associations

questions.question: For a commercial bank, if a current or retired staff member dies, which family members qualify for the additional staff interest?
questions.answer: The spouse of a deceased current or retired staff member qualifies, but the staff member’s children, including minors, do not.
questions.evidence:
(ii) the spouse of a deceased member or a deceased retired member of the bank’s staff; and

Note: Children (including minor) are not eligible for additional interest admissible to deceased member of the bank’s staff.

unanswerable.question: For a commercial bank, what minimum balance must a staff member maintain in a savings account to qualify for the additional 1% interest?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph specifies no minimum account balance or balance-maintenance condition for eligibility for the additional staff interest.

questions.question: When must a commercial bank treat a deceased depositor's NRE term deposit as a domestic rupee term deposit at maturity?
questions.answer: This treatment applies when the claimants of the deceased depositor's NRE term deposit are residents.
questions.evidence: In case the claimant(s) of an NRE term deposit account of a deceased depositor are residents, the deposit on maturity shall be treated as a domestic rupee term deposit and interest shall be paid for the subsequent period at a rate applicable to a domestic term deposit of similar maturity.

questions.question: At what rate must a commercial bank pay interest after maturity on a deceased depositor's NRE term deposit when the claimants are residents?
questions.answer: Interest must be paid at the rate applicable to a domestic term deposit of similar maturity.
questions.evidence: interest shall be paid for the subsequent period at a rate applicable to a domestic term deposit of similar maturity.

unanswerable.question: What numerical interest rate should a commercial bank use for the post-maturity period on a deceased depositor's NRE term deposit when the claimants are residents?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph refers to the rate applicable to a domestic term deposit of similar maturity but does not state any numerical interest rate.

questions.question: If a commercial bank accepts an FCNR(B) term deposit without informing the depositor of the penalty components, who must bear the exchange loss from a premature withdrawal?
questions.answer: The commercial bank must bear the exchange loss arising from the premature withdrawal.
questions.evidence: (1) The components of penalty shall be clearly brought to the notice of the depositors at the time of acceptance of the deposits. If not, the exchange loss arising out of premature withdrawal shall be borne by the bank.

questions.question: Can a commercial bank impose a penalty to recover swap costs when a depositor prematurely withdraws an FCNR(B) term deposit?
questions.answer: Yes. The bank may, at its discretion, levy a penalty to recover the swap cost.
questions.evidence: (4) A bank shall, at its discretion, levy penalty to recover the swap cost in the case of premature withdrawal of FCNR(B) deposits.

unanswerable.question: What penalty percentage or fixed fee amount must a commercial bank apply for premature withdrawal of an FCNR(B) term deposit?
unanswerable.why: The rule requires a comprehensive, Board-approved penalty policy and disclosure of its components, but it does not specify any penalty rate, fixed fee amount, or calculation formula.

questions.question: For a commercial bank, if an FCNR(B) deposit is renewed within 14 days of maturity, counting both dates, which interest rate should it pay on the renewed deposit?
questions.answer: The bank should pay the lower of the appropriate rate for the renewal period prevailing on the original maturity date and the rate prevailing when the depositor seeks renewal.
questions.evidence: does not exceed 14 days, the rate of interest payable on the amount of the deposit so renewed shall be the appropriate rate of interest for the period of renewal as prevailing on the date of maturity or on the date when the depositor seeks renewal, whichever is lower.

questions.question: For a commercial bank authorised under FEMA, 1999, may it recover overdue-period interest if a renewed FCNR(B) deposit is withdrawn before the minimum stipulated period is completed?
questions.answer: Yes. The bank may, at its discretion, recover the interest paid for the period beyond the original maturity date.
questions.evidence: If, after renewal, the deposit is withdrawn before completion of the minimum stipulated period under the Scheme, a bank authorised under FEMA, 1999, may, at its discretion, recover the interest paid for the overdue period, i.e., period beyond the original date of maturity.

unanswerable.question: For a commercial bank, what minimum period must a renewed FCNR(B) deposit be held after renewal before an early withdrawal can result in recovery of the overdue-period interest?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph refers to the minimum stipulated period under the Scheme but does not specify its duration, so the required period cannot be determined from it.

questions.question: Under the RBI’s deposit interest-rate rules for commercial banks, under what circumstances must a commercial bank refrain from charging a penalty for premature withdrawal of a term deposit?
questions.answer: The commercial bank must not levy the penalty when depositors of a branch covered by paragraph 7(9) request premature withdrawal because the business is being transferred to another bank.
questions.evidence: No penalty for premature withdrawal shall be levied, where depositors of the branch of a bank as mentioned in paragraph 7(9) of these Directions desire premature withdrawal of deposit consequent to the transfer of business to another bank.

questions.question: Does the no-penalty treatment for premature withdrawal by commercial bank depositors apply to every branch whose business is being transferred, or only to branches identified in paragraph 7(9)?
questions.answer: It applies only to branches of a bank mentioned in paragraph 7(9), and only when the premature withdrawal is consequent to the transfer of business to another bank.
questions.evidence: No penalty for premature withdrawal shall be levied, where depositors of the branch of a bank as mentioned in paragraph 7(9) of these Directions desire premature withdrawal of deposit consequent to the transfer of business to another bank.

unanswerable.question: How many days in advance must depositors notify a commercial bank branch of their intention to withdraw a term deposit early because the branch’s business is being transferred to another bank?
unanswerable.why: Paragraph 25 states the condition for the no-penalty treatment but does not specify any notice period or advance-notice requirement.

questions.question: Under the RBI’s rules for commercial banks, is it mandatory to give eligible retired senior citizen employees the additional senior-citizen interest rate?
questions.answer: No. A commercial bank may, at its discretion, provide the additional interest rate to qualifying retired staff members.
questions.evidence: A bank may, at its discretion, give its resident Indian retired staffs, who are senior citizens, the benefit of additional interest rates as admissible to senior citizens over and above the additional interest payable to them by virtue of their being retired members of the bank’s staff.

questions.question: Which retired bank employees qualify for the additional senior-citizen interest rate paid by a commercial bank?
questions.answer: The employee must be a retired member of the bank’s staff, a resident Indian, and a senior citizen.
questions.evidence: A bank may, at its discretion, give its resident Indian retired staffs, who are senior citizens, the benefit of additional interest rates as admissible to senior citizens

unanswerable.question: What is the maximum additional interest rate, in percentage points, that a commercial bank may pay to a retired senior citizen employee under the RBI’s domestic deposit interest rules?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph permits a discretionary additional senior-citizen interest rate but does not state any numerical rate, percentage-point limit, or cap.

questions.question: For a deceased foreign currency non-resident (FCNR(B)) depositor, must a commercial bank pay interest when converting the account into an RFC or resident rupee account if the minimum maturity period has not yet been completed?
questions.answer: Yes, subject to the conditions in paragraph 7, the bank must pay interest at the time of conversion even if the deposit has not completed the minimum maturity period.
questions.evidence: Subject to the conditions given in paragraph 7 of these Directions, a bank shall pay interest at the time of conversion of FCNR(B) Account into RFC / Resident Rupee Account even if the deposit has not completed the minimum maturity period mentioned in paragraph 32(2)(i) above.

questions.question: What limit applies to the interest rate a commercial bank may pay when converting a deceased depositor’s FCNR(B) account into an RFC or resident rupee account?
questions.answer: The interest rate must not exceed the rate payable on savings bank deposits held under the RFC Account Scheme.
questions.evidence: the rate of interest shall not exceed the rate payable on savings bank deposits held under RFC Account Scheme.

unanswerable.question: What exact minimum maturity period must a commercial bank require for an FCNR(B) deposit before converting it into an RFC or resident rupee account?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph permits conversion before the minimum maturity period is completed but does not state the period’s length; it only refers to paragraph 32(2)(i).

questions.question: Which foreign currency funding sources may a commercial bank use for granting pre-shipment credit in foreign currency (PCFC)?
questions.answer: A commercial bank may fund PCFC with foreign currency borrowed under Notification No. FEMA.3(R)/2018-RB dated December 17, 2018, and with foreign currency generated through buy-sell swaps in the domestic forex market.
questions.evidence: The bank shall use foreign currency funds borrowed in terms of Notification No. FEMA.3(R)/2018-RB dated December 17, 2018 as also foreign currency funds generated through buy-sell swaps in the domestic forex market for granting pre-shipment credit in Foreign Currency (PCFC)

questions.question: What prudential condition must a commercial bank satisfy when granting pre-shipment credit in foreign currency from these permitted funding sources?
questions.answer: The bank must adhere to the Aggregate Gap Limit (AGL) set out in the Master Direction on Risk Management and Inter-Bank Dealings.
questions.evidence: subject to adherence to Aggregate Gap Limit (AGL) in terms of Master Direction - Risk Management and Inter-Bank Dealings.

unanswerable.question: What interest rate may a commercial bank charge on export credit in foreign currency?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph only specifies the permitted foreign currency funding sources and the AGL condition for PCFC. Although it carries the heading 'F.3 Interest on Export Credit in Foreign Currency', it states no interest rate, ceiling, or pricing condition for export credit in foreign currency.

questions.question: What must a commercial bank do to oversee the use of rupee pre-shipment credit provided to exporters?
questions.answer: It must monitor the end-use of the funds, particularly whether inputs are distributed by exporters or main processor units to farmers for raising crops under the arrangements made by them.
questions.evidence: The bank shall also monitor the end-use of funds, viz. distribution of the inputs by the exporters to the farmers for raising the crops as per arrangements made by the exporter / main processor units.

questions.question: Whose arrangements should a commercial bank consider when checking the distribution of inputs to farmers under rupee pre-shipment credit?
questions.answer: The bank should consider the arrangements made by the exporter or main processor unit.
questions.evidence: The bank shall also monitor the end-use of funds, viz. distribution of the inputs by the exporters to the farmers for raising the crops as per arrangements made by the exporter / main processor units.

unanswerable.question: How frequently must a commercial bank monitor the end-use of rupee pre-shipment credit provided to exporters?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph requires monitoring but does not specify any monitoring frequency, interval, or deadline.

questions.question: Under the RBI’s Commercial Banks – Credit Facilities Directions, 2025, which borrowers must disclose an aging schedule of overdue payables in their periodic returns to a commercial bank?
questions.answer: All corporates and other constituent borrowers whose turnover exceeds the threshold fixed by the commercial bank’s Board of Directors must disclose the aging schedule of overdue payables in their periodical returns to banks.
questions.evidence: all corporates and other constituent borrowers having turnover above threshold level as fixed by the bank’s Board of Directors shall be mandated to disclose ‘aging schedule’ of their overdue payables in their periodical returns submitted to banks.

questions.question: For a commercial bank, who fixes the turnover threshold used to determine which borrowers must disclose overdue payables in periodic returns?
questions.answer: The commercial bank’s Board of Directors fixes the turnover threshold above which the disclosure requirement applies.
questions.evidence: all corporates and other constituent borrowers having turnover above threshold level as fixed by the bank’s Board of Directors shall be mandated to disclose ‘aging schedule’ of their overdue payables in their periodical returns submitted to banks.

unanswerable.question: What turnover amount must a corporate borrower exceed to be required by a commercial bank to disclose the aging schedule of overdue payables?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph requires the bank’s Board of Directors to fix the threshold but does not state any turnover amount, formula, or minimum level.

questions.question: A commercial bank is asked to fund an exporter who is paid from overseas by cheque or draft rather than by electronic transfer. What must the bank confirm before granting export credit to an exporter with a good track record?
questions.answer: The bank must satisfy itself that the remittance is against an export order, follows trade practices for the goods concerned, and is an approved method of realising export proceeds under extant rules.
questions.evidence: after satisfying itself that it is against an export order, is as per trade practices in respect of the goods in question and is an approved method of realisation of export proceeds as per extant rules.

questions.question: For an exporter whose overseas buyer remits payment by cheque or draft, up to what point must a commercial bank continue providing export credit?
questions.answer: The bank must continue the export credit until the proceeds of the cheque or draft received from abroad are realised.
questions.evidence: the bank shall grant export credit to exporters of good track record till the realisation of proceeds of the cheque, draft etc. received from abroad

unanswerable.question: What is the maximum amount or percentage of the invoice value that a commercial bank may lend as Rupee Export Packing Credit to a manufacturer supplier whose exports are routed through STC, MMTC, or another export house?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph merely identifies Rupee Export Packing Credit for manufacturer suppliers exporting through STC/MMTC/other export houses and agencies; it states no ceiling, rate, or percentage for such credit.

questions.question: When a commercial bank introduces a new lending product, what must it consider regarding the customer's needs and circumstances?
questions.answer: The bank must take into account customer suitability and appropriateness when introducing any product.
questions.evidence: the bank while introducing any kind of product shall take into account the customer suitability and appropriateness

questions.question: What must a commercial bank do to ensure its borrowers understand the risks and liabilities associated with a newly launched product?
questions.answer: The bank must ensure that borrowers and customers are made fully aware of the risks and liabilities under such products.
questions.evidence: also ensure that the borrowers / customers are made fully aware of the risks and liabilities under such products.

unanswerable.question: Within what time period must a commercial bank communicate the risks and liabilities of a newly introduced product to its borrowers?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph requires that borrowers and customers be made fully aware of the risks and liabilities of products, but it does not specify any deadline or time period for doing so.

questions.question: Can a commercial bank sanction a real-estate loan before the borrower obtains the required clearances, and if so, when may it disburse the loan?
questions.answer: Yes, the proposal may be sanctioned in the normal course, but disbursement must wait until the borrower has obtained the requisite clearances from government authorities.
questions.evidence: In order that the loan approval process is not hampered on account of this, while the proposals could be sanctioned in normal course, the disbursements shall be made only after the borrower has obtained requisite clearances from the government authorities.

questions.question: During a commercial bank's appraisal of a real-estate loan, what must the bank ensure the borrower has obtained?
questions.answer: The bank must ensure that the borrower has obtained prior permission for the project from government, local governments, or other statutory authorities, wherever required.
questions.evidence: While appraising loan proposals involving real estate, the bank shall ensure that the borrowers obtain prior permission from government / local governments / other statutory authorities for the project, wherever required.

unanswerable.question: How long after a borrower obtains the requisite clearances may a commercial bank delay disbursement of a real-estate loan?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph does not specify any maximum waiting period or deadline for disbursement after the clearances are obtained.

questions.question: When a commercial bank finances a specific housing or development project, what must the builder/developer/company disclose in the project's pamphlets or brochures?
questions.answer: The builder/developer/company must disclose the name(s) of the bank(s) to which the property is mortgaged.
questions.evidence: (1) the builder / developer / company shall disclose in the Pamphlets / Brochures etc., the name(s) of the bank(s) to which the property is mortgaged.

questions.question: For a specific housing or development project financed by a commercial bank, can the bank release funds if the builder/developer/company has not complied with the required mortgage-disclosure requirements?
questions.answer: No. The commercial bank must ensure compliance with the stipulated terms and conditions and must not release funds unless the builder/developer/company fulfils those requirements.
questions.evidence: (4) The bank shall ensure compliance of the above terms and conditions and funds shall not be released unless the builder / developer / company fulfils the above requirements.

unanswerable.question: When financing a specific housing or development project, what percentage of the loan must a commercial bank withhold until the builder/developer/company complies with the mortgage-disclosure requirements?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph prohibits releasing funds until the requirements are fulfilled, but it does not specify any withholding percentage or other numerical limit.

questions.question: Must a commercial bank refrain from entering into lease agreements departmentally with equipment leasing companies and other NBFCs engaged in equipment leasing?
questions.answer: Yes. A commercial bank must not enter into lease agreements departmentally with equipment leasing companies, and the restriction also extends to other NBFCs engaged in equipment leasing.
questions.evidence: they shall not enter into lease agreements departmentally with such companies as well as other NBFCs engaged in equipment leasing.

questions.question: Can a commercial bank extend financial assistance to an equipment leasing company?
questions.answer: Yes. Banks can extend financial assistance to equipment leasing companies, provided they do not enter into lease agreements departmentally with them.
questions.evidence: As banks can extend financial assistance to equipment leasing companies

unanswerable.question: What is the maximum amount a commercial bank may lend to an equipment leasing company?
unanswerable.why: The rule does not specify any monetary cap, exposure limit, or deadline for financial assistance to equipment leasing companies; it only addresses the prohibition on departmental lease agreements.

questions.question: For a commercial bank participating in the Export Bills Abroad Rediscounting Scheme, can an amount arising from export bills rediscounted with recourse in the domestic market be counted as export credit by the rediscounting bank?
questions.answer: No. The rediscounting bank must not count the amount as export credit; only the first bank that discounted the bills may reflect it.
questions.evidence: Bills rediscounted ‘with recourse’ in the domestic market could get reflected only in the case of the first bank discounting the bills as that bank alone will have recourse to the exporter and the bank rediscounting shall not reckon the amount as export credit.

questions.question: Under the Export Bills Abroad Rediscounting Scheme, does the commercial bank rediscounting export bills with recourse in the domestic market have recourse to the exporter, or does the first discounting bank retain it?
questions.answer: The first bank that discounted the bills has recourse to the exporter; the rediscounting bank does not.
questions.evidence: that bank alone will have recourse to the exporter and the bank rediscounting shall not reckon the amount as export credit.

unanswerable.question: What maximum percentage of a commercial bank's export credit may be reflected through rediscounting under the Export Bills Abroad Rediscounting Scheme?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph explains which bank may reflect rediscounted bills and which bank retains recourse, but it states no percentage or numerical limit.

questions.question: For a commercial bank, what is the maximum annual household income allowed for a collateral-free loan to qualify as a microfinance loan under the RBI's Commercial Banks – Credit Facilities Directions, 2025?
questions.answer: The household's annual income must be up to ₹3,00,000.
questions.evidence: A microfinance loan is defined as a collateral-free loan given to a household having annual household income up to ₹3,00,000.

questions.question: Under the RBI's Commercial Banks – Credit Facilities Directions, 2025, which family members are included when a commercial bank assesses whether a borrower is a household for a microfinance loan?
questions.answer: The household is an individual family unit consisting of the husband, wife and their unmarried children.
questions.evidence: For this purpose, the household shall mean an individual family unit, i.e., husband, wife and their unmarried children.

unanswerable.question: Under the RBI's Commercial Banks – Credit Facilities Directions, 2025, what documents must a commercial bank require from a borrower to verify household income for a microfinance loan?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph defines microfinance loans and the meaning of household, but it does not specify any documentation or income-verification requirements.

questions.question: What must a commercial bank maintain for project finance under the project finance database requirements?
questions.answer: The bank must capture and maintain project-specific data in an electronic and easily accessible format on an ongoing basis, covering at least the debtor profile, original project profile, changes in the date of commencement of commercial operations (DCCO), credit events other than deferment of DCCO, and the current specification of the project.
questions.evidence: Project specific data, in electronic and easily accessible format, shall be captured and maintained by the bank on an ongoing basis.

questions.question: What information must a commercial bank record in its project finance database when a project's date of commencement of commercial operations (DCCO) is changed?
questions.answer: The bank must record the date of change and the reason for it, the extended DCCO, revised project debt and total project cost, the increase in cost and cost overrun, the percentage of the total increase financed by equity and by debt, and the revised D/E, DSCR, repayment tenor, repayment start date, repayment frequency and external credit rating.
questions.evidence: Date of Change, reason for change, extended DCCO, revised project debt, revised project total cost, increase in cost, cost overrun, % of total increase financed by equity, % of total increase financed by debt, revised D/E, revised DSCR, revised repayment tenor, revised repayment start date, revised repayment frequency, revised external credit rating.

unanswerable.question: How long must a commercial bank retain project finance database records after a project loan is repaid or the project is closed?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph requires project-specific data to be captured and maintained on an ongoing basis but states no retention period, archival deadline, or record-disposal condition after repayment or project closure.

questions.question: As a compliance officer at a commercial bank, which forms of Default Loss Guarantee (DLG) are we allowed to accept?
questions.answer: A commercial bank may accept DLG only in one or more of three forms: cash deposited with the bank, a fixed deposit maintained with a Scheduled Commercial Bank with a lien marked in favour of the bank, or a bank guarantee in favour of the bank.
questions.evidence: A bank shall accept DLG only in one or more of the following forms: (1) Cash deposited with the bank. (2) Fixed Deposit maintained with a Scheduled Commercial Bank with a lien marked in favour of the bank. (3) Bank Guarantee in favour of the bank.

questions.question: Can a commercial bank accept a Default Loss Guarantee in the form of a fixed deposit held with another Scheduled Commercial Bank, and what condition has to be satisfied for that to be acceptable?
questions.answer: Yes, but the fixed deposit must be maintained with a Scheduled Commercial Bank and a lien must be marked in favour of the commercial bank that is accepting the DLG.
questions.evidence: (2) Fixed Deposit maintained with a Scheduled Commercial Bank with a lien marked in favour of the bank.

unanswerable.question: What minimum percentage of the credit exposure must a commercial bank require from the borrower as Default Loss Guarantee (DLG)?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph only lists the permitted forms of DLG (cash, fixed deposit with a lien, and bank guarantee) and does not state any minimum percentage, amount, or quantum of DLG relative to the facility.

questions.question: As a commercial bank providing digital banking services, which laws and legal requirements must the bank continuously comply with, and where must legal settlement take place?
questions.answer: The bank must continuously comply with the Information Technology Act, 2000, the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023, and other legal requirements. Legal settlement must be within India.
questions.evidence: The provisions (as amended from time to time) of the Information Technology Act, 2000, Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023, and other legal requirements. The jurisdiction of legal settlement would be within India.

questions.question: When a commercial bank uses digital banking to transfer a customer’s funds for cash payout to a recipient, which DPSS circulars must it follow?
questions.answer: It must follow the DPSS circulars on the July 24, 2024 review of the domestic money transfer framework and the October 05, 2011 relaxations, as issued and amended from time to time.
questions.evidence: conditions stipulated in the circulars on ‘Domestic Money Transfer – Review of Framework dated July 24, 2024’ and ‘Domestic Money Transfer- Relaxations dated October 05, 2011’ as issued and amended from time to time by the Department of Payment and Settlement Systems (DPSS), Reserve Bank.

unanswerable.question: For a commercial bank offering digital banking channels, how frequently must it conduct an internal audit to verify compliance with the digital banking requirements?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph requires continuous adherence but does not specify an internal-audit frequency, review cycle, or deadline.

questions.question: Can a commercial bank require a customer to register for digital banking before issuing a debit card?
questions.answer: No. A commercial bank must not make digital banking registration mandatory for customers who wish to obtain another banking facility, such as a debit card.
questions.evidence: Banks shall not make it mandatory for the customer to opt for any digital banking channel to avail any other banking facility like debit cards.

questions.question: What information must a commercial bank include in the terms and conditions given to a customer registering for digital banking services?
questions.answer: The terms must cover any applicable charges and the circumstances in which they apply, the timeframe and process for stop-payment instructions, helpdesk and grievance-redressal details, and the customer's risks, responsibilities and liabilities.
questions.evidence: These shall provide details of charges (if any) to be levied under specific circumstances, timeframe and process to initiate stop-payment instructions, helpdesk details, grievance redressal, and risks, responsibilities, and liabilities of customers.

unanswerable.question: What daily transaction limit must a commercial bank impose on a customer's digital banking transactions?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph requires banks to set transaction and velocity limits according to their risk perception and to follow any stricter RBI or payment-system requirements, but it does not prescribe a specific daily amount or number.

questions.question: As a commercial bank offering digital banking services, which RBI cybersecurity framework must we apply, and do we need to track subsequent amendments to it?
questions.answer: We must apply the Cyber Security Framework in Banks (DBS.CO/CSITE/BC.11/33.01.001/2015-16 dated June 02, 2016), and follow it as amended from time to time.
questions.evidence: DBS.CO/CSITE/BC.11/33.01.001/2015-16 dated June 02, 2016 – Cyber Security Framework in Banks, as amended from time to time.

questions.question: What ongoing compliance duty does a commercial bank offering digital banking services have under the general guidelines, and does it vary with the type of digital banking facility provided?
questions.answer: The bank must comply on a continuous basis with the Directions in the general guidelines chapter. This duty applies regardless of the type of digital banking facility offered.
questions.evidence: All banks offering digital banking services, regardless of type of facility, shall comply with the Directions contained in this chapter on a continuous basis.

unanswerable.question: Within what period must a commercial bank report a cyber security incident affecting its digital banking channels to the RBI under the Cyber Security Framework in Banks?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph merely identifies the Cyber Security Framework in Banks as an applicable instruction and states no incident-reporting timeline, deadline, or escalation condition.

questions.question: Do the RBI's Digital Banking Channels Authorisation Directions, 2025 apply to a scheduled commercial bank?
questions.answer: Yes. The Directions apply to Commercial Banks, which for this purpose cover banking companies other than Small Finance Banks, Payment Banks, and Local Area Banks, along with corresponding new banks and the State Bank of India.
questions.evidence: These Directions shall be applicable to Commercial Banks (hereinafter collectively referred to as 'banks' and individually as a 'bank').

questions.question: Is the State Bank of India covered by the RBI's Digital Banking Channels Authorisation Directions, 2025?
questions.answer: Yes. The State Bank of India is expressly included within the definition of Commercial Banks for the purposes of these Directions, alongside banking companies (other than Small Finance Banks, Payment Banks, and Local Area Banks) and corresponding new banks.
questions.evidence: For the purpose of these Directions, ‘Commercial Banks’ mean banking companies (other than Small Finance Banks, Payment Banks, and Local Area Banks), corresponding new banks, and the State Bank of India, as defined respectively under clauses (c), (da), and (nc) of Section 5 of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949.

unanswerable.question: What is the deadline for a commercial bank to apply to the RBI for authorisation to offer digital banking channels under the 2025 Directions?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph only identifies which lenders the Directions apply to and defines Commercial Banks; it states no application deadlines, time periods, or authorisation timelines.

questions.question: As a compliance officer at a commercial bank, what should I do if I find that a borrower's accounts have been falsified and the borrower's statutory auditor was negligent or deficient in conducting the audit?
questions.answer: The bank should consider lodging a formal complaint against the borrower's statutory auditor with the NFRA or ICAI so that the auditor's accountability can be examined. Pending disciplinary action, the complaint should also be forwarded to the RBI's Department of Supervision at the Central Office and to the IBA, after satisfying itself of the auditor's involvement, giving the auditor an opportunity to be heard, and suitably recording the procedure followed.
questions.evidence: In case any falsification of accounts on the part of the borrowers is observed by a bank, and the auditors are found to be negligent or deficient in conducting the audit, the bank shall consider lodging a formal complaint against the statutory auditors of the borrowers with the National Financial Reporting Authority (NFRA) / Institute of Chartered Accountants of India (ICAI)

questions.question: Can a commercial bank appoint its own auditor to certify whether a borrower is diverting or siphoning loan funds, instead of depending on the borrower's statutory auditor?
questions.answer: Yes. A commercial bank is free to engage its own auditors for a specific certification on diversion or siphoning of funds without relying on certification given by the borrower's auditor. It may also award a separate mandate to the borrower's auditors for this purpose, provided appropriate covenants are incorporated in the loan agreements to enable such a mandate.
questions.evidence: In addition to the above and with a view to preventing diversion / siphoning of funds by the borrowers, a bank is free to engage their own auditors for such specific certification without relying on certification given by borrowers' auditor.

unanswerable.question: What is the minimum account outstanding amount above which a commercial bank must commission a forensic audit of a wilful defaulter's affairs and books of accounts?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph only requires the bank to fix a threshold in its own board-approved policy and to consider commissioning a forensic audit depending on the nature of the wilful default and the quality of evidence; it states no specific monetary amount, limit, or deadline.

questions.question: Under the RBI's Commercial Banks – Treatment of Wilful Defaulters and Large Defaulters Directions, 2025, when may a commercial bank remove a borrower's name from the LWD list if the account is resolved under the IBC or the RBI's resolution framework for stressed assets?
questions.answer: The name may be removed after the resolution plan is implemented, provided the resolution results in a change in the management and control of the entity or business enterprise.
questions.evidence: shall be removed from the LWD after implementation of the resolution plan under IBC or the Reserve Bank of India (Commercial Banks – Resolution of Stressed Assets) Directions, 2025.

questions.question: Under the RBI's Commercial Banks – Treatment of Wilful Defaulters and Large Defaulters Directions, 2025, do the penal measures continue to apply to the erstwhile promoters and directors of a wilful defaulter after a resolution plan is implemented under the IBC?
questions.answer: Yes. Penal measures under Paragraph 7(3)(ii) and (iii) continue to apply to erstwhile promoters, directors, guarantors and persons in charge of the entity's affairs, and also to entities they are associated with in those capacities.
questions.evidence: The penal measures detailed in Paragraph 7 (3) (ii) and (iii) shall continue to apply to the erstwhile promoter(s) / director(s) / guarantor(s) / persons who were in charge and responsible for the management of the affairs of the entity / business enterprise

unanswerable.question: Under the RBI's Commercial Banks – Treatment of Wilful Defaulters and Large Defaulters Directions, 2025, within how many days must a commercial bank remove a wilful defaulter's name from the LWD list after implementing a resolution plan under the IBC?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph requires removal from the LWD after implementation of the resolution plan but does not state any time limit, number of days, or other deadline for completing that removal.

questions.question: Must a commercial bank report guarantors who fail to honour their commitments when those commitments are invoked, and how should they be classified?
questions.answer: Yes. The commercial bank must report them to credit information companies as large defaulters or wilful defaulters, as applicable.
questions.evidence: A bank shall report to credit information companies the details of guarantors who have failed to honour the commitments thereunder when invoked, as large defaulters / wilful defaulters, as the case may be.

questions.question: Which annexes must a commercial bank follow when reporting guarantors who fail to honour invoked commitments?
questions.answer: The commercial bank must report the details in accordance with Annex I and Annex II.
questions.evidence: The details shall be reported as per Annex I and II.

unanswerable.question: Within how many days must a commercial bank report a guarantor who has failed to honour an invoked commitment to credit information companies?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph requires reporting but does not specify any reporting deadline or number of days.

questions.question: Under the RBI's 2025 directions for commercial banks on wilful defaulters and large defaulters, which entities qualify as commercial banks for the purpose of the rules?
questions.answer: The covered category comprises all banking companies, corresponding new banks, and the State Bank of India, as defined under section 5 of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949.
questions.evidence: For the purpose of these Directions, ‘Commercial banks’ mean all banking companies, corresponding new banks and State Bank of India as defined under subsections (c), (da) and (nc) of section 5 of the Banking Regulation Act,1949.

questions.question: Under the RBI's 2025 directions for commercial banks on wilful defaulters and large defaulters, do the restrictions on further financial accommodation to wilful defaulters and the large-defaulter provisions cover all RBI-regulated entities, including those not defined as a lender?
questions.answer: Yes. They apply to every entity regulated by the Reserve Bank, regardless of whether it falls within the directions' definition of a lender.
questions.evidence: The restrictions on further financial accommodation to wilful defaulters and provisions regarding large defaulters contained in these Directions, shall apply to all entities regulated by the Reserve Bank, irrespective of whether they fall within the definition of ‘lender’ as provided in these Directions or not.

unanswerable.question: What monetary threshold defines a large defaulter under the RBI's 2025 directions for commercial banks?
unanswerable.why: The applicability provisions do not state any monetary threshold or borrower-exposure criterion for classifying a borrower as a large defaulter.

questions.question: For a commercial bank, can a borrower's name be removed from the Large Wilful Defaulter (LWD) list after only part of a compromise settlement is paid, if the remaining balance falls below ₹25 lakh?
questions.answer: No. The name must remain on the LWD list until the compromise amount is paid in full, even if the outstanding balance falls below ₹25 lakh or the threshold notified by the RBI.
questions.evidence: Till such time as only part payment is made, name of the borrower shall not be removed from the LWD even if the outstanding amount becomes less than the threshold of ₹25 lakh or as notified by Reserve Bank of India from time to time.

questions.question: If a commercial bank cancels a compromise settlement because the borrower did not follow its terms and changes the amount recoverable, what amount should it use when reporting the wilful defaulter?
questions.answer: The bank must report with reference to the revised amount payable by the borrower.
questions.evidence: In cases where a bank decides to cancel a compromise settlement due to non-adherence to the terms of the settlement and revises the amount payable by the borrower, the reporting shall be with reference to the revised amount.

unanswerable.question: How soon must a commercial bank remove a borrower's name from the LWD list after the compromise amount has been paid in full?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph makes full payment the condition for removal but does not specify any deadline for removing the name or completing the reporting after full payment.

questions.question: What legal backing allows a commercial bank to share borrower credit information with credit information companies?
questions.answer: CICRA provides the statutory backing for a commercial bank (a CI) to share credit information with credit information companies, subject to the conditions stipulated in CICRA.
questions.evidence: The CICRA provides statutory backing for sharing of credit information by a CI with CICs, subject to conditions stipulated therein.

questions.question: Does a commercial bank still need to obtain a borrower's consent before reporting that borrower's credit information to credit information companies?
questions.answer: No. With CICRA in force, the requirement of a consent clause has become redundant, so a commercial bank need not insist on obtaining consent from borrowers.
questions.evidence: Therefore, with CICRA coming into force, the requirement of a ‘consent clause’ has become redundant and a CI need not insist upon obtaining such consent from borrowers.

unanswerable.question: Within what time period must a commercial bank report a borrower's credit information to credit information companies after CICRA comes into force?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph explains that CICRA provides statutory backing for credit information sharing and that the borrower consent clause is redundant, but it states no reporting deadline or time period.

questions.question: Which credit information companies are registered with the Reserve Bank of India under Section 5 of the CICRA for the commercial bank credit information reporting framework?
questions.answer: The registered CICs are CRIF Credit Information Services Private Limited, Equifax Credit Information Services Private Limited, Experian Credit Information Company of India Private Limited, and TransUnion CIBIL Limited.
questions.evidence:
1. | CRIF Credit Information Services Private Limited | November 25, 2010
2. | Equifax Credit Information Services Private Limited | March 26, 2010
3. | Experian Credit Information Company of India Private Limited | February 17, 2010
4. | TransUnion CIBIL Limited | March 05, 2012

questions.question: For a commercial bank subject to the RBI credit information reporting framework, what does the term “Specified User (SU)” mean?
questions.answer: A Specified User has the meaning assigned under clause (l) of section 2 of the CICRA and includes those notified under regulation 3 of the Credit Information Companies Regulations, 2006, as amended from time to time.
questions.evidence: ‘Specified User (SU)’ shall have the same meaning assigned to it under clause (l) of section 2 of CICRA and those notified under regulation 3 of the Credit Information Companies Regulations, 2006, hereinafter referred to as “CIC Regulations” (as amended from time to time).

unanswerable.question: What minimum annual turnover or asset-size threshold qualifies a commercial bank as a Specified User under the RBI credit information reporting framework?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph defines “Specified User” by reference to clause (l) of section 2 of the CICRA and regulation 3 of the CIC Regulations, but it states no turnover or asset-size threshold.

questions.question: As a compliance officer at a commercial bank, how far in advance must the convenor of the Standing Sub-Group of TWG circulate the meeting agenda and notes?
questions.answer: The convenor must send the agenda and notes at least 15 days before the scheduled meeting.
questions.evidence: the convenor shall send the meeting agenda and notes at least fifteen (15) days before the scheduled meeting.

questions.question: At a commercial bank, what must a member of the Standing Sub-Group of TWG do if it wants the meeting to consider a new issue?
questions.answer: The member should send the convenor a note outlining the points for discussion and proposed solutions.
questions.evidence: if members desire to introduce a new issue or item for discussion, they should send a note outlining the points of discussion and proposed solutions to the convenor.

unanswerable.question: How many days before a Standing Sub-Group of TWG meeting must a commercial bank member send the convenor a note proposing a new issue?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph specifies a 15-day advance period only for the convenor’s meeting agenda and notes; it does not state any deadline for a member’s note proposing a new issue.

questions.question: As a commercial bank financing self-help groups (SHGs), above what group-loan amount must we report members' credit information, and what must happen for smaller SHGs?
questions.answer: Member-level credit reporting is required for SHGs whose group loans exceed ₹1,00,000. Members of all SHGs, regardless of the group-loan amount, must still provide non-credit information through the SHG when it approaches the bank for a loan.
questions.evidence: The collection and reporting of credit information in respect of SHG members will be restricted to the members of those SHGs that take loans exceeding ₹1,00,000/-. However, the members of all SHGs, regardless of the amount of group loan, shall report the non-credit information to CIs through the SHG Group

questions.question: As a commercial bank financing SHGs, what NPA conditions require us to collect detailed information from members whose loans exceed ₹20,000?
questions.answer: The bank must collect the detailed information if the gross NPA in its SHG segment exceeds 10% or is more than 5 percentage points above the bank's overall gross NPA. The bank must also monitor SHG-segment NPA levels continuously.
questions.evidence: A CI shall monitor the NPA levels in the SHG segment on an ongoing basis and collect detailed information from SHG members availing loans exceeding a lower threshold of ₹20,000, if the Gross NPA in the SHG segment exceeds 10% or is higher than the gross NPA of the CI by 5 percentage points.

unanswerable.question: Within how many days must a commercial bank submit SHG member-level data to credit information companies after collecting it from the members?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph requires the collection and reporting of SHG member data but does not specify any reporting deadline or number of days for submission to credit information companies.

questions.question: For a private sector bank (PVB), at what age must its MD&CEO/CEO or whole-time director (WTD) stop continuing in that role?
questions.answer: The role must end by age 70; no person may continue as the MD&CEO/CEO or WTD beyond 70 years.
questions.evidence: No person shall continue as the MD&CEO / CEO or WTD of a PVB beyond the age of 70 years.

questions.question: May a private sector bank's board set a retirement age below 70 for its whole-time directors, including the MD&CEO/CEO?
questions.answer: Yes. The board may prescribe a lower retirement age through its internal policy, provided the overall limit of 70 years is respected.
questions.evidence: Within the overall limit of 70 years, as part of its internal policy, an individual PVB's Board is free to prescribe a lower retirement age for the WTDs, including the MD&CEO / CEO.

unanswerable.question: What prior RBI approval or reporting steps are required when a private sector bank's MD&CEO/CEO reaches age 70?
unanswerable.why: The provision states only the upper age limit and the board's freedom to prescribe a lower internal retirement age; it specifies no RBI approval or reporting requirement.
